SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/r1.claim: Al Imran’s account of changing events uses active verbs; al-Anam instead foregrounds God's attributes and power with nominal and participial forms, then uses a verb for the living’s movement. Each form suits its context.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/r1.anchor: فالسياق كله حركة وتغيير وتبديل فجاء بالصغية الفعلية الدالة على التحدد والتغيير والحركة

BURHAN:v4p108/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p108/r6.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v4p108/r6.claim: Ibn Malik parses ومخرج الميت as coordinated with يخرج because the noun can be interpreted as a verb.

STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r17.claim: Verses 95–99 discuss God as giver of life and death in this world and the next.
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r17.anchor: Vv. 95–99 discuss God as the giver of both life and death, in this world and the next

SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r1.claim: The annexation may be genuine, with فالق as an active participle meaning a past act already completed; Abdullah’s reading فلق as a past verb supports this.
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r1.anchor: على أنه اسم فاعل بمعنى الماضي لأن ذلك قد كان

SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r2.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r2.claim: Abdullah reads فلق as a past-tense verb, evidence for construing the annexation as genuine.
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r2.anchor: ويدل عليه قراءة عبد الله " فلق " فعلا ماضيا

SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r3.claim: The annexation may instead be non-genuine, with a present or future sense narrated as occurring now; الحب is genitive in form but accusative in position.
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الإضافة غير محضة على أنه بمعنى الحال أو الاستقبال، وذلك على حكاية الحال

SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r4.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r4.claim: الفلق means splitting; al-Raghib qualifies it as separating one part from another.
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r4.anchor: والفلق: هو شق الشيء، وقيده الراغب بإبانة بعضه من بعض

SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r5.claim: Other lexical senses of فلق include a hollow between rises, what God taught Moses to split the sea, morning, rivers as in 27:61, a thing split open, a marvel, and gaps between mountains or camel humps; 113:1 is cited.

SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r6.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r6.claim: Some gloss فالق as خالق; an objection says this is not a known lexical sense, but the author dismisses it because Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak report it and al-Farra gives فطر, خلق, and فلق as synonyms.
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r6.anchor: وفسر بعضهم " فالق " هنا بمعنى خالق، قيل: ولا يعرف هذا لغة، وهذا لا يلتفت إليه لأن هذا منقول عن ابن عباس والضحاك

SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r7.claim: النوى is a collective whose singular is نواة, like قمح/قمحة; it also means distance, and نوت البسرة/أنوت describes a date whose stone has hardened.

SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r8.claim: The final radical of نواة is yāʾ because its middle radical is wāw; the author notes that the forms more often differ.
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r8.anchor: ولام " النواة " ياء لأن عينها واو، والأكثر التغاير.

SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r9.claim: يخرج may be an independent sentence with no syntactic position, or a second nominative predicate of إن.

SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari coordinates ومخرج with فالق: God is described by the two predicates ‘splitter’ and ‘bringer out’; يخرج keeps its parse as clarification if independent.
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r10.anchor: أنه معطوف على فالق - ولم يذكر الزمخشري غيره - أي: الله فالق ومخرج

SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r11.claim: Alternatively, ومخرج coordinates with يخرج; the parse converts the noun and verb into each other’s sense as needed.
SAMIN-DURR:6:95/r11.anchor: معطوفا على " يخرج " ، وهل يجعل الفعل في تأويل اسم

SAMIN-DURR:6:95#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:95#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:95#2/r1.claim: The cited poems illustrate coordinating a noun with a verb when the verb is construed as a noun, or the noun as a verb.

SAMIN-DURR:6:95#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:95#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:95#2/r2.claim: Two further examples are يا رب بيضاء من العواهج أم صبي قد حبا أو دارج and بات يغشيها بعضب باتر يقصد في أسوقها وجائر, glossed respectively as حاب and قاصد.
SAMIN-DURR:6:95#2/r2.anchor: يا رب بيضاء من العواهج أم صبي قد حبا أو دارج

ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r1.claim: Fa-annā tuʾfakūn means, From where are you turned away from the truth?
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r1.anchor: أي فمن أين تصرفون عن الحق.

ASAD-NOTES:6:95#n80/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:95#n80/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:95#n80/r1.claim: Asad links this verse to his note 90 on 5:90.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p643/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p643/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p643/r1.claim: A noun indicates permanence while a verb indicates renewal and movement; accordingly the living is brought out with a verb, while the dead is brought out with a noun for stillness.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p643/r1.anchor: الاسم يدل على الثبوت والفعل يدل على الحدوث والتجدد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p643/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p643/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p643/r2.claim: The wording matches the qualities attributed here: movement characterizes life and stillness characterizes death.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p643/r2.anchor: أبرز صفات الحيّ الحركة والتجديد (من الحياة) وقد قال تعالى مع الحيّ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p904/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p904/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p904/r2.claim: The noun conveys constancy and the verb renewal; the verb with the living evokes motion, while the noun with the dead evokes stillness.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p904/r2.anchor: استعمل صيغة الفعل لأن أبرز صفات الحيّ هي الحركة واستعمل صيغة الإسم مع الميت

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r1.claim: Tafṣīl originates in separating things; it can mean broad explanation or the presentation of several distinct matters.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r1.anchor: التفصيل هو إما أن يكون التبيين والفصل هو الحجز بين الشيئين وهذا الأصل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r2.claim: The passage moves across separate subjects—seeds, dawn, sun and moon, then stars—so its many different signs are appropriately called tafṣīl.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r2.anchor: إنتقل من الحب والنوى إلى الإصباح ثم الشمس والقمر ثم النجوم، مواضيع أخرى ثم ينتقل يذكر أموراً كثيرة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.claim: The words ḥabb and nawā mean seed and fruit-stone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.anchor: The words ﺣﺐand ﻧــﻮى mean “seed and fruit-stone.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.claim: The signs are introduced through small things before moving to larger ones.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.anchor: The mention of God’s signs begins with small things and then the larger ones are referred to.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.claim: God splits seeds and stones, drawing out their contents through stages until a plant becomes a tree, which displays His power.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.anchor: It is God’s power and might that is responsible to rent asunder seeds and fruit-stones

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.claim: God gives each seed and stone its potential and orders the earth, sky, winds, clouds, and seasons to nurture its growth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.anchor: by ordering the earth, the heavens, the winds, the clouds and the seasons to play their roles and nurture them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.claim: Every seed bears witness that its creator also schemed the universe as a whole.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.anchor: every seed that grows from this earth, by its every existence, bears witness that it has come into existence

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.claim: The coordinated growth of a seed rules out independent gods governing separate domains.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p82/.anchor: If this universe was being governed by different gods and they would have been independent in their own spheres

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.claim: The phrase also appears with slight variation in 6:37, where Islahi says it is explained.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.anchor: have been mentioned with slight variation in verse 37, where they have been explained

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.claim: The phrase describes lifeless mango stones and wheat seeds producing living plants, which later yellow, decay, and wither.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.anchor: From the lifeless fruit-stones of mangoes and from the lifeless seeds of wheat, a luxuriant tree and a lush green plant sprouts

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.claim: The same recurring pattern of life and death is visible in humans and animals.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.anchor: The same observation can be made in human beings and animals.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.claim: Nations and peoples also follow a recurring rise-and-fall pattern, sometimes dominating the world before disappearing.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.anchor: So much so, it is the same with nations and peoples: they follow a perpetual pattern of rise and fall.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.claim: No one escapes the universal law of life and death, rise and fall.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.anchor: No one can escape this law of life and death, rise and fall.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.claim: If another being governed the universe, it should be able to cancel this law somewhere in creation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.anchor: If someone besides God was also governing this universe, why can he not annul this law in even a part of the universe.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.claim: A cosmos arising from matter or an unbridled force should have persisted without interruption or change.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.anchor: a manifestation of matter or an unbridled power, then this manifestation should have continued and perpetuated

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.claim: The first clause uses a verb depicting an occurrence, while the second uses a fāʿil form conveying decision and intent.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.anchor: in the first expression (bringing forth the living from the dead), a verb is used which portrays a situation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.claim: Living beings do not choose death, yet nature makes every living being die; this shows that God alone has authority.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.anchor: once life is acquired no living being is prepared to consign itself to death but such is the relentless law of nature that every living being must die.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.claim: Al-Wāqiʿah 56:86–87 similarly challenges people to restore a dying person's life if they are not subordinate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.anchor: 86-87 of S ūrah al-Wāqi‘ah, it is similarly stated

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.speaker: people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.claim: Some people limit the phrase to the old egg-or-hen question; Islahi reads it instead as natural laws of life and death.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.anchor: Generally people have confined these words to the age old question of what came first: the egg or the hen.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.claim: Read with 6:102, the clause may omit its predicate, understood from the statement that God is their Lord.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.anchor: in the first sentence the enunciative (khabar) is suppressed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.claim: If taken as complete without ellipsis, the clause means that all this is God's benevolence, so where can people turn away?
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p83/.anchor: it would mean that all this is a benevolence of God; then where do you turn away.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.claim: The Arabs acknowledged God as creator of everything while still associating partners with Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.anchor: everything; however, at the same time, they associated partners with Him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.claim: Since God creates and controls everything, people should worship and obey Him alone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.anchor: when all this is God’s creation and control, then people should worship Him and show obedience to Him alone

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.claim: Although people take an initial step toward truth, their intellect deserts them, they turn aside, and the truth they gained is lost.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.anchor: if they take the first step in the right direction, the next diverges from the straight path and the truth that had been gained is forever lost.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.claim: Though the verse concerns monotheism, the observable emergence of life from death also subtly points to resurrection after death.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.anchor: This verse though occurs clearly in the context of monotheism, but it also subtly points to the hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.claim: If seeds and fruit-stones can emerge from earth after decay, there is no reason to wonder that humans will rise from burial.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.anchor: If after decaying and decomposing, seeds and a fruit-stones can once again emerge from the earth, why can’t human beings after being buried in the earth once again rise from it?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.claim: Dawn splitting darkness parallels God's splitting a fruit-stone to bring forth a tree.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.anchor: Just as He creates a tree by splitting a fruit-stone, He also brings forth the dawn after slicing through the veil of darkness.

NASHR:v1p199/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p199/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p199/r1.claim: The fourth articulation point is the lower throat near the mouth, producing ghayn and khāʾ.

NASHR:v1p199/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p199/r2.speaker: شريح
NASHR:v1p199/r2.claim: Shurayḥ places ghayn before khāʾ; Makkī places khāʾ first, while Ibn Khurūf says Sibawayh did not intend an ordering for sounds from one point.
NASHR:v1p199/r2.anchor: ونص شريح على أن الغين قبل

NASHR:v1p199/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p199/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p199/r3.claim: The six letters from the three throat articulation points are collectively called throat letters.
NASHR:v1p199/r3.anchor: وهذه الستة الأحرف المختصة بهذه الثلاثة المخارج هي الحروف الحلقية

NASHR:v1p199/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p199/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p199/r4.claim: Qāf is articulated at the rear of the tongue against the upper palate; Shurayḥ instead locates it at the uvula toward the throat and khāʾ's point.
NASHR:v1p199/r4.anchor: أقصى اللسان مما يلي الحلق وما فوقه من الحنك

NASHR:v1p199/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p199/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p199/r5.claim: Kāf comes from the tongue slightly below qāf and the palate; both are called uvular sounds because the uvula lies between mouth and throat.
NASHR:v1p199/r5.anchor: أقصى اللسان من أسفل مخرج القاف

NASHR:v1p199/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p199/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p199/r6.claim: Jīm, šīn, and non-lengthened yāʾ come from the middle tongue and palate and are called shajariyya; reported ordering differs among scholars.
NASHR:v1p199/r6.anchor: من وسط اللسان بينه وبين وسط الحنك

NASHR:v1p199/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p199/r7.speaker: المهدوي
NASHR:v1p199/r7.claim: Al-Mahdawī puts shīn after kāf, and jīm and yāʾ after shīn; another report puts jīm first.
NASHR:v1p199/r7.anchor: وقال المهدوي: إن الشين تلي الكاف، والجيم والياء يليان الشين

NASHR:v1p199/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p199/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p199/r8.claim: Ḍād comes from the near edge of the tongue against the molars, usually on the left but sometimes on the right; Sibawayh's wording allows both sides.
NASHR:v1p199/r8.anchor: من أول حافة اللسان وما يليه من الأضراس من الجانب الأيسر عند الأكثر، ومن الأيمن عند الأقل وكلام سيبويه يدل على أنها تكون من الجانبين

NASHR:v1p199/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p199/r9.speaker: الخليل
NASHR:v1p199/r9.claim: Al-Khalīl calls ḍād shajariyya because it shares the articulation point of the previous three; for him the ‘tree’ is the opening of the mouth.
NASHR:v1p199/r9.anchor: إنها أيضا شجرية يعني من مخرج الثلاثة قبله

NASHR:v1p199/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p199/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p199/r10.claim: Other scholars define the ‘tree’ as the meeting of the jaws near the chin tuft, so ḍād cannot come from there.

NASHR:v1p199/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p199/r11.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p199/r11.claim: Lām comes from the side of the tongue, from the area nearest its tip through the tip, against the upper palate near the teeth.
NASHR:v1p199/r11.anchor: من حافة اللسان من أدناها إلى منتهى طرفه

NASHR:v1p199/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p199/r12.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p199/r12.claim: Nūn comes from the tongue tip against the area above the incisors, slightly below the lām point.
NASHR:v1p199/r12.anchor: من طرف اللسان بينه وبين ما فوق الثنايا أسفل اللام قليلا

NASHR:v1p199/r13.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p199/r13.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p199/r13.claim: Rāʾ shares nūn's point but is slightly farther back; lām, nūn, and rāʾ are called dhalaqiyya after the tongue tip.
NASHR:v1p199/r13.anchor: من مخرج النون من طرف اللسان بينه وبين ما فوق الثنايا العليا

NASHR:v1p289/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p289/r1.claim: The poet describes camels gathered at their water basin; ʿukūf means turning toward or attending to something.
NASHR:v1p289/r1.anchor: يصف إبلا اعتمدت حوضها لتشرب الماء، والعكوف الإقبال على الشيء

NASHR:v1p289/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p289/r2.claim: In large assimilation, thāʾ assimilates into five letters: tāʾ, dhāl, sīn, shīn, and ṣād.
NASHR:v1p289/r2.anchor: والثاء تدغم في خمسة أحرف، هي: التاء، والذال، والسين، والشين، والصاد

NASHR:v1p289/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r3.speaker: ابن حبش
NASHR:v1p289/r3.claim: Ibn Ḥabash, transmitting from al-Sūsī, articulates the jīm in «أخرج شطأه».
NASHR:v1p289/r3.anchor: فأظهره ابن حبش عن السوسي، وأبو محمد الكاتب

NASHR:v1p289/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r4.speaker: أبو محمد الكاتب
NASHR:v1p289/r4.claim: Abū Muḥammad al-Kātib, through Ibn Mujāhid and Abū al-Zarʿāʾ from al-Dūrī, articulates the jīm in «أخرج شطأه».
NASHR:v1p289/r4.anchor: وأبو محمد الكاتب، عن ابن مجاهد، عن أبي الزعراء عن الدوري

NASHR:v1p289/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r5.speaker: أبو القاسم بن بشار، ومدين
NASHR:v1p289/r5.claim: The transmission of Abū al-Qāsim ibn Bashshār from al-Dūrī and Madīn from his companions preserves clear articulation.
NASHR:v1p289/r5.anchor: وهو رواية أبي القاسم بن بشار، عن الدوري ومدين، عن أصحابه

NASHR:v1p289/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r6.speaker: ابن جبير
NASHR:v1p289/r6.claim: Ibn Jubayr, transmitting from al-Yazīdī, articulates the jīm in «أخرج شطأه».
NASHR:v1p289/r6.anchor: وابن جبير عن اليزيدي،، وابن واقد، عن عباس

NASHR:v1p289/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r7.speaker: ابن واقد
NASHR:v1p289/r7.claim: Ibn Wāqid, through ʿAbbās from Abū ʿAmr, articulates the jīm in «أخرج شطأه».
NASHR:v1p289/r7.anchor: وابن واقد، عن عباس، عن أبي عمرو والخزاعي

NASHR:v1p289/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r8.speaker: الخزاعي
NASHR:v1p289/r8.claim: Al-Khuzāʿī, transmitting from Shujāʿ, articulates the jīm in «أخرج شطأه».
NASHR:v1p289/r8.anchor: والخزاعي، عن شجاع، وأدغمه سائر أصحاب الإدغام

NASHR:v1p289/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r9.speaker: سائر أصحاب الإدغام
NASHR:v1p289/r9.claim: The other transmitters of large assimilation assimilate the jīm in «أخرج شطأه»; al-Dānī and his companions read only this form.
NASHR:v1p289/r9.anchor: وأدغمه سائر أصحاب الإدغام، وهو الذي قرأ به الداني وأصحابه ولم يذكروا غيره

NASHR:v1p289/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p289/r10.claim: Both articulation and assimilation of the jīm in «أخرج شطأه» are sound readings; al-Shadhdhāʾī reports reading both with Ibn Mujāhid.
NASHR:v1p289/r10.anchor: والوجهان صحيحان نص عليهما سبط الخياط ورواهما جميعا الشذائي

NASHR:v1p289/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r11.speaker: الشذائي
NASHR:v1p289/r11.claim: Al-Shadhdhāʾī says he read «أخرج شطأه» assimilated and articulated with Ibn Mujāhid, who formerly used assimilation.
NASHR:v1p289/r11.anchor: ورواهما جميعا الشذائي وقال: قرأت على ابن مجاهد مدغما ومظهرا

NASHR:v1p289/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r12.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p289/r12.claim: Al-Dānī calls jīm-to-tāʾ assimilation harsh because their articulation points are distant, yet permits it through their relation to sīn and shīn.
NASHR:v1p289/r12.anchor: قال الداني: وإدغام الجيم في التاء قبيح لتباعد ما بينهما في المخرج، إلا أن ذلك جائز لكونهما من مخرج السين

NASHR:v1p289/r13.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r13.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن اليزيدي
NASHR:v1p289/r13.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Yazīdī and the other companions report that Abū ʿAmr assimilated jīm into tāʾ and tāʾ into jīm.
NASHR:v1p289/r13.anchor: نصا عن اليزيدي ابنه عبد الرحمن وسائر أصحابه، فقالوا عنه: كان يدغم الجيم في التاء، والتاء في الجيم

NASHR:v1p289/r14.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r14.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p289/r14.claim: The ḥāʾ assimilates into ʿayn only in «فمن زحزح عن النار», where the word is long and repeats ḥāʾ.
NASHR:v1p289/r14.anchor: تدغم في العين في حرف واحد قوله تعالى: فمن زحزح عن النار فقط؛ لطول الكلمة وتكرار الحاء

NASHR:v1p289/r15.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r15.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p289/r15.claim: The ḥāʾ is articulated clearly in the other cited phrases because an impediment prevents assimilation.
NASHR:v1p289/r15.anchor: ولذلك يظهر فيما عداه نحو لا جناح عليكم، والمسيح عيسى، والريح عاصفة، وما ذبح على النصب لوجود المانع

NASHR:v1p289/r16.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p289/r16.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p289/r16.claim: The author reports no disagreement in his transmission for assimilating jīm in «المعارج تعرج» and articulating it in «وأخرج ضحاها» and «مخرج صدق».
NASHR:v1p289/r16.anchor: ولم يختلف عنه أحد من طرفنا في إدغام المعارج تعرج، وإظهار وأخرج ضحاها، ومخرج صدق

NASHR:v2p223/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p223/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p223/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar doubles the yāʾ in all the listed forms of «الميتة/ميتا», «بلد ميت», and «الحي من الميت والميت من الحي».
NASHR:v2p223/r6.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بتشديد الياء في جميع ذلك، ووافقه نافع في يس الأرض الميتة

QIRAAT-ER:6:95:10#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:95:10#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:95:10#1/r1.claim: The light form mayt contrasts with standard mayyit in intensity; mayt can describe something recently dead or not deeply or permanently dead.
QIRAAT-ER:6:95:10#1/r1.anchor: Light form mayt vs. standard mayyit — difference in intensification; mayt may refer to what has recently died

QIRAAT-ER:6:95:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:95:13#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:95:13#1/r1.claim: The light mayt form is repeated here, matching the earlier variant and keeping both occurrences consistently light.
QIRAAT-ER:6:95:13#1/r1.anchor: Light form mayt paralleling the variant at word 10 — consistent lightening across both occurrences

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214#2/r1.claim: Qatada says God splits grain and date stones so that plants emerge from them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فالق الحب والنوى ﴾ قال تفلق الحب والنوى عن النبات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r1.claim: فالق means splitting or cleaving something open.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r2.claim: النوى is a collective noun; its singular is distinguished from it by feminine تاء.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r2.anchor: النوى اسم جنس بينه وبين مفرده تاء التأنيث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r1.claim: The apparent meaning is that God splits every grain to bring out its plant and every kernel to bring out its tree; Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and others agree.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r1.anchor: الظاهر أن المعنى أنه تعالى فالق الحب شاقه فمخرج منه النبات والنوى فمخرج منه الشجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak also explain فالق as خالق, though the source notes that this sense is not known in Arabic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والضحاك أيضا فالق بمعنى خالق قيل ولا يعرف ذلك في اللغة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r3.speaker: تاج القراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r3.claim: Taj al-Qurraʾ treats فطر, خلق, and فلق as synonyms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r3.anchor: وقال تاج القراء: فطر وخلق وفلق بمعنى واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r4.speaker: مجاهد وأبو مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r4.claim: Mujahid and Abu Malik take the phrase to point to the cleft in a wheat grain and in a date kernel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد وأبو مالك: إشارة في الشق الذي في حبة البر ونواة التمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r5.speaker: إسماعيل الضرير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r5.claim: Ismail al-Darir says it means splitting the grain-bearing ear and the date-bearing fruit, and analogous cases.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r5.anchor: وقال إسماعيل الضرير: المعنى فالق ما فيه الحب من السنبل وما فيه النوى من التمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r6.speaker: الماتريدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r6.claim: Al-Maturidi says grain and kernels stand for the world's provisions and replacements, all traced to God as all people are traced to one soul.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r6.anchor: وقال الماتريدي وخصهما بالذكر لأن جميع ما في الدنيا من الأبدال منهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r7.claim: After mentioning resurrection, the splitting of a hard kernel to produce a tender green plant exemplifies God's power and points toward resurrection and gathering after death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r7.anchor: ولما كان قد تقدم ذكر البعث نبه على قدرته تعالى الباهرة في شق النواة مع صلابتها وإخراجه منها نبتا أخضر لينا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r8.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r8.claim: Abdullah reads فالق as the past-tense verb فلق.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r8.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله فالق الحب جعله فعلا ماضيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r9.claim: The noun مُخرج is coordinated with the participle فالق, not with يخرج, because splitting and extracting the living are parallel kinds of action and the first clause explains the second.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r9.anchor: ومخرج الميت على قوله: فالق الحب اسم فاعل على اسم فاعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r10.claim: The same living-from-dead and dead-from-living wording was interpreted earlier in Aal ʿImran; there, two preceding finite clauses make verbal coordination apt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r10.anchor: تقدم تفسير هذا في أوائل آل عمران

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r11.claim: Although a participle can coordinate with a present verb when their meanings match, the poet's participle-versus-verb construction supplies an analogous grammatical example.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r11.anchor: لأنه في معناه كما قال الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r12.speaker: قتادة والضحاك والسدي وغيرهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r12.claim: Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and others say the phrase indicates God's action in splitting every grain and kernel to produce all its plants and trees.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p591/r12.anchor: وبه قال قتادة والضحاك والسدي وغيرهم قالوا: هذه إشارة إلى فعل الله في أن يشق جميع الحب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r1.claim: After establishing proofs of oneness, al-Ālūsī presents these wondrous divine acts as evidence of God's knowledge, power, subtle craftsmanship, and wisdom; all rational, transmitted, and philosophical inquiry ultimately aims at knowing Him in essence, attributes, and acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r1.anchor: شروع في تقرير بعض افاعيله تعالى العجيبة الدالة على كمال علمه تعالى وقدرته ولطيف صنعه وحكمته إثر تقرير أدلة التوحيد

ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk explain fāliq as the one who creates and originates.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r2.anchor: والفالق الموجد والمبدع كما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما والضحاك

ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r3.claim: Ḥabb means grain; nawā is the plural of a date pit, though dictionaries give it masculine and feminine forms and the plurals anwāʾ and nuwāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r3.anchor: والحب معلوم والنوى جمع نواة التمر كما في القاموس وغيره يؤنث ويذكر ويجمع على أنواء ونوى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r4.claim: The Imam broadens nawā to the object inside any fruit, while common unqualified use means a date pit and other fruits' pits are specified by name.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r4.anchor: وفسره الامام بالشيء الموجود في داخل الثمرة بالمثلثة أعم من التمر بالمثناة وغيره والمشهور أن النوى إذا إطلق فالمراد منه ما في القاموس

ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r5.claim: Falaq literally means splitting; calling God the splitter who creates reflects the mind's image of nonexistence as unbroken darkness split open when a thing is brought into being.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r5.anchor: وأصل الفلق الشق وكان إطلاق الفالق على الموجد باعتبار أن العقل يتصور من العدم ظلمة متصلة لا انفراج فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r6.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and al-Suddī explain the phrase as splitting dry seed and pit to bring forth plants, palms, and trees; most commentators adopt this reading, which al-Ālūsī considers preferable.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r6.anchor: وعن الحسن وقتادة والسدي أن المعنى شاق الحبة اليابسة ومخرج النبات منها وشاق النواة ومخرج النخل والشجر منها وعليه أكثر المفسرين ولعله الأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r7.claim: The emergence displays perfect power through the wonders of creation, figured as birds sounding through boughs of wisdom and streams overflowing in gardens of generosity.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r7.anchor: وفي ذلك دلالة على كمال القدرة لما فيه من العجائب التي تصدح اطيارها على أفنان الحكم وتطفح أنهارها في رياض الكرم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r8.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r8.claim: Mujāhid and Abū Mālik say fāliq means the fissure in grains and pits, which God created in that form, like a cistern narrow at its mouth and wide below; al-Ālūsī weakens this because it shows less clearly God's power.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r8.anchor: وعن مجاهد وأبي مالك أن المراد بالفلق الشق الذي بالحبوب وبالنوى أي أنه سبحانه خالقهما كذلك كما في قولك

ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r9.claim: One analysis coordinates the active participle with fāliq rather than with yukhṛiju, since yukhṛiju explains the preceding phrase and this clause does not; the source notes that participle and verb can nevertheless be coordinated.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226/r9.anchor: وهذا عند بعض عطف على ( فالق ) لا على ( يخرج الحي ) الخ لأنه كما علمت بيان لما قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r1.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Munīr coordinates the two clauses, arguing their frequent paired use in the present tense makes a syntactic break unlikely; the present vividly pictures bringing life from death, a more striking sign and the first stage in the order of events.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r1.anchor: واختار ابن المنير كونه معطوفا على

ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī cites the verse about rain making the earth green and a ghoul-fighting poem as examples of using the present tense to bring an action vividly before the listener.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r2.anchor: بأني قد لقيت الغول يسعى يسهب كالصحيفة صحصحان فآخذه وأضربه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r3.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r3.claim: The Imam says verbs convey renewed action and concern at every moment, whereas participles indicate a continuing state; since bringing forth life is nobler, its verbal form marks greater divine attention, while the coordination remains sound because the two forms can substitute for each other.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r3.anchor: وقال الامام في وجه ذلك الاختلاف : إن لفظ الفعل يدل على أن الفاعل معتن بالفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r4.speaker: عبد القاهر
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r4.claim: ʿAbd al-Qāhir's examples contrast God's continually giving provision, expressed with a verb, with the dog remaining in its posture, expressed with a participle.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p226#2/r4.anchor: ما ذكره الشيخ عبد القاهر في دلائل الاعجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r1.claim: If life and death are literal terms for beings with or without perception and power, applying them to plants, trees, fresh shoots, and pits requires a general metaphor or a combination of literal and metaphorical senses.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r1.anchor: فلابد من القول بعموم المجاز أو الجمع بين المجاز والحقيقة على مذهب من يرى صحته إن قلنا إن الحي حقيقة فيمن يكون

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r2.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r2.claim: The Imam treats bringing fresh tender growth from dry seed and dry seed from living growth as metaphorical applications; Ibn ʿAbbās instead explains the two directions as believer from unbeliever and unbeliever from believer.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r2.anchor: فانه جعل ما نقل عن الزجاج أن المعنى يخرج النبات الغض الطري من الحب اليابس ويخرج الحب اليابس من النبات الحي النامي

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the phrase as God bringing a believer from an unbeliever and an unbeliever from a believer.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r3.anchor: كالمروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما من أن المعنى يخرج المؤمن من الكافر والكافر من المؤمن

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r4.claim: That powerful one of manifest proof is God, the necessary existent, uniquely deserving worship.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r5.claim: The question means: how can you be turned from worshipping God alone to associating powerless beings with Him? The implication is that this should be impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r5.anchor: فكيف تصرفون عن عبادته وتشركون به من لايقدر على شيء لا سبيل إلى ذلك أصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r6.speaker: الصاحب بن عباد
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbād argues that human acts are not created by God, since it would be unfitting for God to ask how people are turned away if He created their turning; al-Ālūsī refers readers to his earlier answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227/r6.anchor: وتمسك الصاحب بن عباد بهذا على أن فعل العبد ليس مخلوقا لله تعالى لأنه سبحانه لو خلق فيه الافك لم يلق به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والسدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r1.claim: Faliq means splitting the seed from its stalk and the pit from the palm so each can emerge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r1.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة والسدي: معناه يشق الحبة عن السنبلة والنواة عن النخلة فيخرجها منها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r2.claim: Al-habb is the collective term for seeds and grains such as wheat, barley, and maize, and things without pits.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r2.anchor: والحب جمع الحبة، وهي اسم لجميع البذور والحبوب من البر والشعير والذرة، وكل ما لم يكن له نوى،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r3.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God splits dry seeds and pits to bring out green leaves.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: يشق الحبة اليابسة والنواة اليابسة فيخرج منها أوراقا خضرا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r4.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r4.claim: Mujahid takes the splitting to refer to their two clefts: grain is split to produce plants and pits to produce palms.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يعني الشقين اللذين فيهما، أي: يشق الحب عن النبات ويخرجه منه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r5.claim: Nawa is the plural of nawat, referring to pits such as those of dates, apricots, and peaches.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r5.anchor: والنوى جمع النواة، وهي كل ما لم يكن حبا، كالتمر والمشمش والخوخ ونحوها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r6.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets faliq as creator of grain and pits.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك: فالق الحب والنوى يعني: خالق الحب والنوى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r7.claim: God brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r7.anchor: يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي ذلكم الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r8.claim: Tؤفكون means that people are turned away from the truth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170/r8.anchor: ذلكم الله فأنى تؤفكون} تصرفون عن الحق.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r1.claim: God splits grain and date stones to produce plants and trees; another explanation takes the phrase as the actual cleft in wheat and a date stone.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r1.anchor: بالنبات والشجر. وقيل المراد به الشقاق الذي في الحنطة والنواة

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r2.claim: The living means growing animals and plants, matching what precedes; the dead means non-growing things such as sperm drops and seeds.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r2.anchor: يريد به ما ينمو من الحيوان والنبات ليطابق ما قبله

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r3.claim: The dead brought out of the living are those same non-growing things produced from animals and plants.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r4.claim: The nominal form 'bringing out' matches 'splitter'; the preceding verbal 'brings out the living' functions as an explanation of it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r4.anchor: ومخرج ذلك من الحيوان والنبات، ذكره بلفظ يالاسم حملا على فالق الحب

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r5.claim: The one who gives life and death is the one alone deserving worship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r5.anchor: أي ذلكم المحيي المميت هو الذي يحق له العبادة

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:95/r6.claim: The question rebukes those who turn away from God toward another.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r1.claim: The cited promise that God’s blessings cannot be counted frames the signs of creation discussed here.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r1.anchor: 77 ( { وإن تعدوا نعمت الله لا تحصوها } ) 77 [ إبراهيم : 34 ]

BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r2.claim: Splitting seeds and date stones to bring forth plants is a kind of enlivening and displays God’s repeated care.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r2.anchor: ولما كان فلقهما عن النبات من جنس الإحياء لما فيه من النمو فسر معنى الفلق وبينه إشارة إلى الاعتناء به وقتا بعد وقت

BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r3.claim: Living growth includes plants, trees, birds, and animals emerging from seeds, date stones, eggs, and semen; this is an argument against denying resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r3.anchor: أي كالنجم والشجر والطير والدواب { من الميت } من الحب والنوى والبيض والنطف

BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r4.claim: The active participle signals a stable, undisputed fact, unlike the preceding verb that expresses renewed action.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r4.anchor: معبرا باسم الفاعل الدال على الثبات لأنه لا منازعة لهم فيه , فلم تدع حاجة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r5.claim: God also brings dead matter, such as seeds, out of living plants and other living things, further clarifying His power to produce opposites.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r5.anchor: أي من الحب وما معه { من الحي } أي من النجم وما معه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r6.claim: Bringing forth opposites prevents attributing their production to nature or inherent properties, which might seem plausible if each thing produced only its own kind.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r6.anchor: لئلا يتوهم - لو كان لا يخرج عن شيء إلا مثله - أن الفاعل الطبيعة والخاصية

BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r7.claim: Only God can perform these acts; no alleged partner can match Him in any shared divine action, so only He deserves divinity.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r7.anchor: ولا مكافئ له سبحانه وتعالى في شيء من الأشياء فلا شريك له بوجه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r8.claim: The question asks how, and from what direction, people are turned away from the belief they ought to hold.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r4.claim: The account from splitting dawn onward elaborates the earlier statement that God splits grain and kernels, establishing power, oneness, and resurrection before returning to denounce idolatry.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r4.anchor: وكان هذا كله في قوله { فالق الإصباح } شرحا لآية { إن الله فالق الحب والنوى }

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706/r2.claim: The splitting of grain and kernels elaborates God’s creation of the heavens and earth, while the surrounding passage rejects assigning Him partners.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706/r2.anchor: فلما ذكر إبداعه السماوات والأرض بقوله

BURSEVI:v3p55/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55/r1.claim: Falq means splitting something apart; al-habb denotes grain seeds such as wheat, barley, and corn, which God splits to bring out a green shoot.
BURSEVI:v3p55/r1.anchor: الحب : جمع حبة وهي اسم لجميع البزور المقصودة

BURSEVI:v3p55/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55/r2.claim: Nawā is the hard pit inside fruits such as peaches, apricots, and dates; God splits it to bring out a leafy, branch-bearing tree.
BURSEVI:v3p55/r2.anchor: واحدتها نواة وهي الشيء الموجود في داخل الثمر مثل نواة الخوج والمشمش

BURSEVI:v3p55/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55/r3.claim: In context, God brings growing life in animals and plants from non-growing things such as sperm and seeds.
BURSEVI:v3p55/r3.anchor: بيان لما قبله أي يخرج ما ينمو من الحيوان والنبات مما لا ينمو من النطفة والحب

BURSEVI:v3p55/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55/r4.claim: Conversely, God brings non-growing sperm and seeds from living animals and plants; 'living' and 'dead' are metaphors for growing and inert, though life literally entails sensation and voluntary motion.
BURSEVI:v3p55/r4.anchor: فالحي والميت مجاز عن النامي والجامد

BURSEVI:v3p55/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55/r5.claim: Some instead take the words literally: God brings a living human from dead sperm and a dead egg from a living chicken.
BURSEVI:v3p55/r5.anchor: ومنهم من حمل اللفظ على الحقيقة وقال يخرج من النطفة الميتة بشرا حيا ومن الدجاجة بيضة ميتة

BURSEVI:v3p55/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v3p55/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says God brings a believer from an unbeliever, an unbeliever from a believer, a disobedient person from an obedient one, a scholar from an ignorant person, and an intelligent person from a fool, and vice versa.
BURSEVI:v3p55/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : يخرج المؤمن

BURSEVI:v3p55/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55/r7.claim: The palm of faith grows from the dead seeds of the letters in the declaration of divine oneness, while the deadness of hypocrisy emerges from that same living declaration.
BURSEVI:v3p55/r7.anchor: يخرج نخل الإيمان من نوى الحروف الميتة في كلمة لا إله إلا الله

BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r1.claim: That refers to the One of great power and stature, God alone, who deserves worship.

BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r2.claim: The phrase asks how people can be turned away from worshipping God to another; ifk means to invert or turn something aside, and the address is to Quraysh because the sura is Meccan.
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r2.anchor: والإفك في اللغة قلب الشيء وصرفه والخطاب لكفار قريش

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the fāliq of grain and date stones as their creator.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : ان الله فالق الحب والنوى يقول : خلق الحب والنوى

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r2.claim: Qatada says God splits the grain and date stones open so that plants emerge.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : فالق الحب والنوى قال : يفلق الحب والنوى عن النبات

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the fāliq of grain and date stones as their creator.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك : ان الله فالق الحب والنوى قال : خالق الحب والنوى

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r4.claim: Mujahid says the phrase refers to the two clefts within grain and date stones.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد : قوله : ان الله فالق الحب والنوى : الشقان اللذان فيهما

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r5.claim: Al-Suddi explains God splits the grain from its ear and the date stone from its palm.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r5.anchor: عن السدى : قوله : فالق الحب والنوى فالق الحبة عن السنبلة ، قوله : والنوى فالق النواة عن النخلة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r6.claim: A report describes Khalida bint al-Aswad visiting the Prophet, who asks who she is and says, Glory be to God who brings the living from the dead.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r6.anchor: عن الزهري عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله ان خالدة بنت الاسود بن عبد يغوت دخلت على رسول الله

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r7.speaker: عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r7.claim: Umar explains bringing the living from the dead as bringing a believer from a disbeliever; Salman transmits the statement.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r7.anchor: عن سلمان قال : قال عمر : يخرج الحي من الميت ، يخرج المؤمن من الكافر

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r8.claim: Another report says Khalida was a righteous woman whose father was an unbeliever, and the Prophet praised God as the one who brings the living from the dead.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1351/r8.anchor: عن الزهري ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دخل على بعض نسائه فاذا بامراة حسنة الهيئة ، فقال : من هذه ؟ فقالت : خالدة بنت الاسود

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r1.claim: He explains that God brings a human being out of a sperm drop.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : يخرج الحي من الميت قال : يخرج من النطفة بشرا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود، وأبو سعيد الخدري، وسعيد بن جبير، ومجاهد، والنخعي، وقتادة، والضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r2.claim: These authorities are reported to give the same human-from-sperm interpretation.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r2.anchor: وروى عن ابن مسعود وابي سعيد الخدري وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد والنخعي وقتادة والضحاك نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r3.claim: He gives the date palm from its kernel and the ear of grain from its seed as examples of life from the lifeless.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r3.anchor: عن أبي مالك : قوله : يخرج الحي من الميت ، قال : النخلة من النواة ، والسنبلة من الحبة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r4.claim: He cites an egg, lifeless though it comes from a living animal, from which a living creature then emerges.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة : يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي قال : البيضة تخرج من الحي وهي ميتة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r5.speaker: عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r5.claim: As relayed by Salman, Umar says God kneaded Adam's clay for forty days, distinguished and mixed good and evil, and made Adam from it; believers emerge from unbelievers and unbelievers from believers.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r5.anchor: عن ابى عثمان عن سلمان قال : قال عمر : خمر الله عز وجل طينة ادم اربعين يوما

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r6.claim: Hasan and Qatada are reported to give the same believer-from-unbeliever and unbeliever-from-believer interpretation.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r6.anchor: وروى عن الحسن وقتادة نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r7.speaker: إبراهيم عن عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r7.claim: He explains the lifeless thing brought from the living as the dead sperm drop emitted by a living man.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r7.anchor: عن إبراهيم عن عبد الله : قوله : ومخرج الميت من الحي قال : يخرج النطفة الميتة من الرجل الحي

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير والنخعي والضحاك والسدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r8.claim: These authorities are reported to give the same dead-sperm-from-a-living-man interpretation.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r8.anchor: وروى عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير والنخعي والضحاك والسدى نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r9.claim: People come from lifeless sperm, and the same life-from-death pattern applies to livestock and plants.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1352/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد : قوله : يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي قال : الناس الاحياء من النطف

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r1.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r1.claim: He says the kernel comes from the date palm and the seed from the ear of grain.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r1.anchor: عن أبي مالك في قوله : ومخرج الميت من الحي ، وقال : النواة من النخلة ، والحبة من السبنلة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r2.claim: He again explains the dead from the living by an egg that comes from a living animal while lifeless.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة ، قوله : ومخرج الميت من الحي قال : البيضة تخرج من الحي وهي ميتة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس : انى تؤفكون ، انى قال : كيف

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r4.claim: He explains the question as asking how they are turned away.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r4.anchor: عن معمر عن الحسن فانى تؤفكون ، قال : انى تصرفون

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس : قوله : تؤفكون قال : تكذبون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r1.claim: The passage shifts from earlier proofs of oneness, resurrection, and messengership to visible wonders of creation, proving God's sole divinity and disproving Arab idolatry, and a fortiori materialist denial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r1.anchor: استئناف ابتدائي انتقل به من تقرير التوحيد والبعث والرسالة وأفانين المواعظ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r2.claim: The address reproaches the polytheists for ingratitude, while giving believers knowledge, certainty, deeper knowledge of their Lord, and greater gratitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r2.anchor: وفيه علم ويقين للمؤمنين من المصدقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r3.claim: Although no one denies that God performs these acts, the subtle inference from plant growth to resurrection was neglected; the polytheists' denial makes their state like doubt, warranting emphasis with inna.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r3.anchor: كان حالهم كحال من أنكر أو شك في أن الله فالق الحب والنوى ، فأكد الخبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r4.claim: The nominal sentence marks this description as enduring and essential to God; it is an attribute of action or of power and its relations in the terminology of those who deny action-attributes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r4.anchor: وجيء بالجملة الاسمية للدلالة على ثبات هذا الوصف دوامه لأنه وصف ذاتي لله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r5.claim: The sentence does not express exclusivity, because its immediate purpose is to show God's power to bring life from death, not to make a restrictive assertion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r5.anchor: لم يؤت في هذا الخبر بما يقتضي الحصر إذ ليس المقام مقام القصر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r6.claim: Falaq is splitting or cleaving parts apart; here it is the cleft from which shoots and roots of plants and trees emerge, displaying divine knowledge, power, and wisdom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386#2/r6.anchor: والفلق : شق وصدع بعض أجزاء الشيء عن بعض ، والمقصود الفلق الذي تنبثق منه وشائج النبت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r1.claim: Al-habb is a collective noun for what plants yield, singular habba; al-nawa is a collective noun for fruit stones, singular nawa, including date and other fruit kernels from which trees grow.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r1.anchor: والحب اسم جمع لما يثمره النبت ، واحده حبة . والنوى اسم جمع نواة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r2.claim: The clause is a second predicate of inna, explaining the seed-splitting as living plant growth from lifeless hard seed, while its broader meaning also includes animals emerging from sperm or eggs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r2.anchor: وجملة : { يخرج الحي من الميت } في محل خبر ثان عن اسم ( إن )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur favors separating the clause without a conjunction: it clarifies the first predicate, or can be a separate broader predicate clarifying it; conjunction is unnecessary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r3.anchor: فلذلك رجح فصل هذه الجملة عن التي قبلها إلا أنها أعم منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r4.claim: Bringing dead from living is the opposite wonder, displaying complete divine power and denying nature's capacity to create; a freely acting agent produces opposites, unlike a natural cause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r4.anchor: لأنه إخبار بضد مضمون { يخرج الحي من الميت } وصنع آخر عجيب دال على كمال القدرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r5.claim: The clause elaborates seed-splitting: plants yield lifeless dried grain and fruits hold lifeless stones; living animals also yield eggs, milk, musk, pearls, and bezoar stones.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r5.anchor: منها حال إثمار النبات والشجر : حبا ييبس وهو في قصب نباته فلا تكون فيه حياة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r6.claim: He prefers connecting this clause to the preceding life-from-death clause as its completion, like the paired clauses about dawn and night in 6:96.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r6.anchor: وقد رجح عطف هذا الخبر لأنه كالتكملة لقوله : { يخرج الحي من الميت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari instead connects the clause to faliq al-habb, since splitting grain produces life from death, not dead from living; Ibn Ashur says the alternative connection is less apparent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p388/r7.anchor: وجعله في ( الكشاف ) عطفا على { فالق الحب } بناء على أن مضمون قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r1.claim: The imperfect verbal clause presents bringing life from death as deliberate, known action that recurs continually rather than coincidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r1.anchor: وقد جيء بجملة : { يخرج الحي من الميت } فعلية للدلالة على أن هذا الفعل يتجدد ويتكرر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r2.claim: The participial clause conveys permanence; together, the two forms make both processes recurring and constant, numerous and intrinsic, with neither process privileged.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r2.anchor: وجيء في قوله : { ومخرج الميت من الحي } اسما للدلالة على الدوام والثبات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r3.claim: The demonstrative sharply identifies the agent of these immense acts, while hinting at the addressees' obtuseness; only this God known by his great name is divine, so the following question results.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r3.anchor: والإشارة ب { ذلكم } لزيادة التمييز وللتعريض بغباوة المخاطبين المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r4.claim: Afk is turning someone away from a place or action; here it asks how the people are turned away from God's oneness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r4.anchor: والأفك بفتح الهمزة مصدر أفكه يأفكه ، من باب ضرب ، إذا صرفه عن مكان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r5.claim: Anna means from where; the question expresses incredulous rejection, since nothing could rightly turn them away from God's oneness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r5.anchor: و ( أنى ) بمعنى من أين . وهو استفهام تعجيبي إنكاري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r6.claim: The verb is passive because no single cause of their turning is identifiable: Satan's whispering, leaders' misguidance, and their own desires combine.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r6.anchor: وبني فعل { تؤفكون } للمجهول لعدم تعين صارفهم عن توحيد الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r7.claim: That is Allah is an independent sentence for reflection, making the ensuing how-are-you-turned-away clause parenthetical.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r7.anchor: وجملة ( ذلكم الله ) مستأنفة مقصود منها الاعتبار ، فتكون جملة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r1.claim: The verse opens an appeal to reflection and continues the prior contrast between God and idols.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r1.anchor: هذا ابتداء تنبيه على العبرة والنظر، ويتصل المعنى بما قبله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r2.speaker: مجاهد وأبو مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r2.claim: Mujahid and Abu Malik mean the cleft in barley grain and date stone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد وأبو مالك هذه إشارة إلى الشق الذي في حبة البر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says that reading restricts the lesson to some grains and stones without reason.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r3.anchor: والعبرة على هذا القول مخصوصة في بعض الحب وبعض النوى،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r4.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة والسدي وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Qatāda, al-Suddī, and others mean God splits every seed for its plant and kernel for its tree.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك وقتادة والسدي وغيرهما هذه إشارة إلى فعل الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers this comprehensive reading as giving the full lesson.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r5.anchor: وهذا هو الظاهر الذي يعطي العبرة التامة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r7.speaker: السدي وأبو مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r7.claim: Al-Suddī and Abu Malik see green plants and trees emerging from dry seeds; greenness is life, dryness death.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r7.anchor: وقال السدي وأبو مالك: يخرج الحي من الميت إشارة إلى إخراج النبات الأخضر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r8.speaker: السدي وأبو مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r8.claim: They see dry matter emerging from plants and trees as the dead from the living.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r8.anchor: ومخرج الميت من الحي إشارة إلى إخراج اليابس من النبات والشجر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others mean living humans from lifeless semen and semen from living humans, likewise animals, birds, fish, and creatures from eggs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره، بل ذلك كله إشارة إلى إخراج الإنسان الحي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers Ibn ʿAbbās's reading; the interpretations are distinct lessons, while the first relies on matching the seed and kernel phrase.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r10.anchor: وهذا القول أرجح وإنما تعلق قائلو القول الأول بتناسب تأويلهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r11.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan means believers from unbelievers and unbelievers from believers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن: المعنى يخرج المؤمن من الكافر والكافر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r12.claim: ‘That is God’ is a subject-predicate construction serving as a warning; fa-annā tuʾfakūn means how are you turned away.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p325/r12.anchor: ذلكم الله ابتداء وخبر متضمن التنبيه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r1.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس، الضحاك، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r1.claim: One interpretation takes faliq to mean creator: God is the creator of grain and date stones.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنه بمعنى الخلق فالمعنى خالق الحب والنوى رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r2.claim: A second interpretation takes faliq in its sense of splitting or cleaving.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r2.anchor: والثاني أن الفلق بمعنى الشق ثم في معنى الكلام قولان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r3.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس، الحسن، السدي، ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r3.claim: On the splitting interpretation, God splits the grain to bring forth its stalk and the date stone to bring forth its palm.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r3.anchor: أنه فلق الحبة عن السنبلة والنواة عن النخلة روى هذا المعنى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r4.speaker: مجاهد، أبو مالك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r4.claim: Another account identifies the cleft as the split running through the grain and the date stone; Ibn al-Saʾib distinguishes grain without a stone, such as wheat and barley, from date stones.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r4.anchor: أنه الشقان اللذان في الحب والنوى قاله مجاهد وأبو مالك قال ابن السائب الحب ما لم يكن له نوى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r5.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi says the phrase about bringing the living from the dead and the dead from the living was explained earlier in Āl ʿImrān, corresponding to 3:27.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p89/r5.anchor: قد سبق تفسير في ال عمران

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90/r1.claim: After this clear proof, how can people be turned away from the truth?
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90/r1.anchor: أي كيف تصرفون عن الحق بعد هذا البيان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r1.claim: God splits grain and pits in the soil so crops grow from varied seeds and fruits of many forms, colors, and tastes from pits.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r1.anchor: أي: يشقه في الثرى فتنبت الزروع على اختلاف أصنافها من الحبوب، والثمار على اختلاف أشكالها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r2.claim: The living plant emerges from the apparently dead, inanimate grain and pit; this is illustrated by 36:33–36.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r2.anchor: أي: يخرج النبات الحي من الحب والنوى، الذي هو كالجماد الميت، كما قال:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r3.claim: The phrase “bringing the dead from the living” is coordinated with “splitter of grain and pit”; Ibn Kathīr says the clause is first explained and then the second coordinated phrase follows.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r3.anchor: وقوله: {ومخرج الميت من الحي} معطوف على {فالق الحب والنوى} ثم فسره ثم عطف عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r4.claim: Among the reported illustrations are a chicken from an egg and an egg from a chicken, or a righteous child from an unbeliever and an unbeliever from a righteous person; the verse encompasses them all.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r4.anchor: بعبارات كلها متقاربة مؤدية للمعنى، فمن قائل: يخرج الدجاجة من البيضة، والبيضة من الدجاجة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r5.claim: God alone, without partner, performs these acts; the verse challenges how people can turn from truth to falsehood and worship others alongside Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304/r5.anchor: ثم قال: {ذلكم الله} أي: فاعل هذه الأشياء هو الله وحده لا شريك له {فأنى تؤفكون}

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r9.claim: Al-ḥabb is the plural of ḥabba and covers grains without pits, such as wheat, barley, and corn.
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r9.anchor: والحب: جمع حبة، وهو كل ما لا يكون له نوى كالبر والشعير والذرة

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r10.claim: Al-nawā is the plural of nawāt and refers to seeds or pits such as those of dates and apricots.
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r10.anchor: والنوى: جمع نواة، وهو كل ما له حب، كالتمر والمشمش

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r11.claim: Ifk is turning away from truth; the term also names overturned places and falsehood because falsehood deviates from truth.
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r11.anchor: والإفك: الانصراف عن الحق والقلب عنه، ومنه: (فأنى يؤفكون)

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r3.claim: In annexation, fāliq drops nunation and al-ḥabb is genitive; with nunation, al-ḥabb is accusative as its object.

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r5.claim: The discourse returns to proving God's oneness to the polytheists through wonders of creation and subtle governance.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r5.anchor: عاد الكلام إلى الاحتجاج على المشركين بعجائب صنعه، ولطائف تدبيره

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r6.speaker: الحسن، وقتادة، والسدي، وابن زيد، وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r6.claim: These authorities explain the phrase as splitting grains so plants grow and splitting pits so palms and trees grow.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r6.anchor: عن الحسن وقتادة والسدي وابن زيد وأبي علي

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk understand fāliq as creator, originator, and bringer into being.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس والضحاك، كأنه ذهب بفالق إلى معنى خالق وفاطر

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r8.claim: Abū Muslim, also identified with Mujāhid's view, takes the phrase as the two clefts in grain and pits and their evenness.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r8.anchor: عن أبي مسلم، وهو قول مجاهد

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r9.claim: Mentioning grains and pits points to complete power and wisdom: plants emerge from their hard shells, grow, and form grain.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r9.anchor: وإنما [خص الحب] والنوى تنبيها على [كمال] قدرته

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r10.claim: Another view treats grain as a sign of provision and pits as a sign of fruit, highlighting God's blessings and sole right to worship.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r10.anchor: وقيل: [أشار بالحب] إلى جنس الأرزاق، وبالنوى إلى جنس الفواكه

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the living from the dead and the dead from the living as a person from sperm and sperm from a person.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r11.anchor: قيل: الإنسان من النطفة، والنطفة من الإنسان

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r12.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r12.claim: Abū ʿAlī gives the example of a bird emerging from an egg and an egg from a bird.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r12.anchor: وقيل: الطير من البيض والبيض من الطير، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r13.speaker: السدي وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r13.claim: Al-Suddī and Abū ʿAlī explain it as a plant emerging from grain and grain from a plant.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r13.anchor: وقيل: النبات من الحب والحب من النبات، عن السدي وأبي علي

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r14.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r14.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets it as a disbeliever from a believer and a believer from a disbeliever.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r14.anchor: وقيل: الكافر من المؤمن، والمؤمن من الكافر

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r15.claim: The person-and-sperm and bird-and-egg explanations are strongest because they take life in its literal sense.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r15.anchor: والأول الوجه، وكذلك الثاني؛ لأنه حمل الكلام على حقيقة الحياة

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r16.claim: The one who creates these things is God, people's Lord and creator, so they should worship Him alone.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r16.anchor: يعني ذاك الذي خلق هذه الأشياء أيها الناس هو الله ربكم وخالقكم

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r17.claim: The signs plainly show the truth, yet people are turned toward falsehood and away from worshipping God.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r17.anchor: أي: تصرفون عن الحق، وتذهب بكم هذه الأدلة الظاهرة إلى الباطل

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r18.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r18.claim: Abū ʿAlī glosses the question as asking how they can make idols into gods.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r18.anchor: وقيل: كيف تكذبون في جعل الأوثان آلهة، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r19.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r19.claim: Al-Aṣamm takes it to ask how they can deny that God will resurrect them and has power to do so.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r19.anchor: وقيل: أنى تكذبون أنه لا يبعثكم بعد الموت، ولا يقدر عليه، عن الأصم

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r20.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r20.claim: Abū Muslim says the passive form follows an Arabic idiom and means: where are you being turned from worshipping God?
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r20.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: وتصرفون وإن كان على ما لم يسم فاعله فهو على مذهب العرب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r1.claim: God splits grain and pits by bringing forth the growing plant and tree.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r2.claim: Mujahid says the phrase means the two clefts in a date pit and a wheat grain.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r2.anchor: وعن مجاهد : أراد الشقين الذين في النواة والحنطة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r3.speaker: author
