KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r3.claim: Living things from dead things include animals and growing things produced from semen, eggs, grain, and pits.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r4.claim: The converse is the production of lifeless seed, grain, and pits from animals and growing things.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r4.anchor: هذه الأشياء الميتة من الحيوان والنامي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r5.claim: Mukh rij is coordinated with fāliq, not the finite verb; the clause about bringing living from dead explains splitting, since growing plants count as living.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r5.anchor: عطفه على فالق الحب والنوى ، لا على الفعل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r6.claim: The author compares this sign of growth with the signs of God’s mercy in the revival of the earth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r6.anchor: ألا ترى إلى قوله : { فانظر إلىءاثار رحمة }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r7.claim: The life-giver and death-causer is God, alone deserving lordship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r7.anchor: هو الله الذي تحق له الربوبية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r8.claim: The question asks how people can turn away from God and devotion to Him toward another.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p45#3/r8.anchor: فكيف تصرفون عنه وعن توليه إلى غيره

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r1.speaker: الحسن، قتادة، السدي، ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r1.claim: These authorities explain splitting grain and date-stone as separating grain from its stalk and pit from its palm.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r1.anchor: يعني فالق الحبة عن السنبلة والنواة عن النخلة , قاله الحسن . وقتادة , والسدي , وابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r2.claim: Mujahid takes al-falaq as the fissure or cleft within the grain and pit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r2.anchor: والثاني : أن الفلق الشق الذي فيهما , قال مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the phrase as creator of grain and date-stones.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r3.anchor: والثالث : أنه يعني خالق الحب والنوى , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r4.speaker: بعض أصحاب الغوامض
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r4.claim: A subtle inward interpretation makes God the revealer of sincerity and hypocrisy contained in the heart's seed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r4.anchor: أنه مظهر ما في حبة القلب من الإخلاص , والرياء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r5.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r5.claim: Al-Suddi explains the living from the dead as a living plant from dead grain and a living palm from a dead pit, and the reverse as grain or pit from plant or palm.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r5.anchor: والنواة الميتة من النخلة الحية , قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets a living person as coming from sperm and sperm as coming from a living person.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r6.anchor: أن يخرج الإنسان من النطفة , والنطفة من الإنسان , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r7.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r7.claim: Hasan understands the living from the dead and dead from living as the believer coming from a disbeliever and vice versa.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r7.anchor: يخرج المؤمن من الكافر , والكافر من المؤمن , قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r8.claim: A further possibility is that God brings an alert, capable person from a dull, helpless one and also the reverse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r8.anchor: وقد ذكرنا فيه احتمالا , أنه يخرج الفطن الجلد من البليد العاجز , ويخرج البليد العاجز من الفطن الجلد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r9.claim: The question means: how can you be turned away from the truth?

MUJAHID:v1p219#5/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p219#5/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p219#5/r1.claim: The 'splitting' refers to the two halves contained within the seed and the date stone.
MUJAHID:v1p219#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ إن الله فالق الحب والنوى ﴾ قال يعني الشقتين اللتين فيهما

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r1.claim: Fāliq al-ḥabb means Creator of grain, including wheat, barley, corn, and all cereals.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r1.anchor: { إن الله فالق الحب } ، يعني خالق الحب، يعني البر، والشعير، والذرة، والحبوب كلها،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r2.claim: Al-nawā covers the pits or stones of fruits such as peaches, jujubes, apricots, grapes, and pears, and every fruit with a pit.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r2.anchor: ثم قال: { والنوى } ، يعني كل ثمرة لها نوى: الخوخ، والنبق، والمشمش، والعنب، والإجاص،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r3.claim: God brings people and animals from dead sperm and birds from dead eggs.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r3.anchor: ثم قال: { يخرج الحي من الميت } ، يقول: أخرج الناس والدواب من النطف وهي ميتة، ويخرج الطير كلها من البيضة وهي ميتة،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r4.claim: Conversely, He brings sperm and eggs from living animals.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r4.anchor: ثم قال: { ومخرج الميت من الحي } ، يعني النطف والبيض من الحي، يعني الحيوانات كلها،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r5.claim: These works are God's alone and demonstrate His oneness through His creation.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r5.anchor: { ذلكم الله } الذى ذكر في هذه الآية من صنعه وحده يدل على توحيده بصنعه،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r6.claim: The question means: how can they deny that God alone has no partner?
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r6.anchor: { فأنى تؤفكون } [آية: 95]، يقول: أنى يكذبون بأن الله وحده لا شريك له.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r1.claim: God splits grain to bring out a stalk and splits the date stone to bring out a palm tree; f-l-q means splitting.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r1.anchor: بالنبات والشجر أى فلق الحب عن السنبلة والنواة عن النخلة والقلق الشق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r2.speaker: مجاهد
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r2.claim: Mujahid takes the reference to be the two clefts in the date stone and the wheat grain.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r2.anchor: وعن مجاهد أراد الشقين اللذين فى النواة والحنطة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r3.claim: The living is the fresh, growing plant that comes from a dry seed.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r3.anchor: ﴿ يخرج الحى من الميت ﴾ النبات الغض النامى من الحب اليابس

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r4.claim: The dead coming from the living may be a dry seed from a growing plant, a human from semen and semen from a human, or a disbeliever from a believer and vice versa.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r4.anchor: الحب اليابس من النبات النامى أو الإنسان من النطفة والنطفة من الانسان أو المؤمن من الكافر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r5.claim: These visible acts of creation answer deniers of resurrection: the One who created them can raise them again.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r5.anchor: فاحتج الله عليهم بما يشاهدونه من خلقه لأنهم أنكروا البعث فاعلمهم أنه الذى خلق هذه الأشياء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r6.claim: Mukhrij is an active participle coordinated with fāliq, not with the finite verb yukhriju.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r6.anchor: لأنه معطوف على فالق الحب لا على الفعل ويخرج الحى من الميت موقعه موقع الجملة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r7.claim: The finite clause explains fāliq: splitting seed and stone to bring out growing life is like bringing the living from the dead.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r7.anchor: المبينة لقوله فالق الحب والنوى لأن فلق الحب والنوى بالنبات والشجر الناميين من جنس إخراج الحى من الميت

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r8.claim: The author cites God's revival of the earth after its death as evidence that growing things count as living.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r8.anchor: لأن النامى فى حكم الحيوان دليله قوله ﴿ ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r9.claim: The one who gives life and death is God, alone deserving lordship rather than the idols.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r9.anchor: ذلكم المحيى والمميت هو الله الذى تحق له الربوبية لا الأصنام

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r10.claim: After such clear evidence, how can people be turned away from God and devotion to Him toward another?
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336/r10.anchor: فكيف تصرفون عنه وعن توليه إلى غيره بعد وضوح الأمر بما ذكرنا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r1.claim: The splitting of grain and stone is a wonder of God's making beyond the idols; a lifeless seed opens into green growth, which produces lifeless seed and stone.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r1.anchor: عد من عجائب صنعه ما يعجز عن أدنى شيء منه آلهتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r2.claim: Hasan and Qatada explain the living-from-dead and dead-from-living as the plant emerging from seed and seed returning from green growth.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r2.anchor: وهذا معنى يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي عن الحسن وقتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak explain faliq as Creator.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والضحاك: معنى فالق خالق

QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r4.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r4.claim: Mujahid says faliq refers to the cleft in a grain or seed.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: عني بالفلق الشق الذي في الحب وفي النوى

QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r5.claim: Nawā is plural of nawāh and applies to the hard stones of fruits such as apricot and peach.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r5.anchor: والنوى جمع نواة، ويجري في كل ما له عجم كالمشمش والخوخ

QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the living-from-dead and dead-from-living as a living human from lifeless sperm and lifeless sperm from a living human.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r6.anchor: يخرج البشر الحي من النطفة الميتة، والنطفة الميتة من البشر الحي عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r7.claim: Dhalikum is parsed as a subject and predicate.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r8.claim: The question means: how can you be turned from truth, given what you see of God's power?
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r8.anchor: فمن أين تصرفون عن الحق مع ما ترون من قدرة الله جل وعز

QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r9.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r9.claim: In Sahih Muslim, Ali swears by the One who split the grain and created the soul that the Prophet covenanted that only a believer loves him and only a hypocrite hates him.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:95/r9.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن علي: والذي فلق الحبة وبرأ النسمة

QASHANI:6:95-96/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:95-96/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:95-96/r1.claim: God splits the heart’s seed through spirit-light into knowledge and gnosis, and the soul’s kernel through heart-light into morals and virtues.
QASHANI:6:95-96/r1.anchor: حبة القلب بنور الروح عن العلوم والمعارف ونوى النفس بنور القلب عن الأخلاق والمكارم

QASHANI:6:95-96/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:95-96/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:95-96/r2.claim: At times the living heart emerges from the dead soul when the spirit’s light overcomes it; at other times, desire and soul-qualities overcome the living heart and return it to death.
QASHANI:6:95-96/r2.anchor: نور الروح عليها { ومخرج } ميت النفس عن حي القلب أخرى

QASHANI:6:95-96/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:95-96/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:95-96/r3.claim: God can turn people through changing states and stages, so the author asks how they turn away from Him to another.
QASHANI:6:95-96/r3.anchor: القادر على تقليب أحوالكم وتغليبكم في أطواركم { فأنى } تصرفون منه إلى غيره

RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r1.claim: After discussing divine unity, prophecy, and related questions, the commentary returns to proofs of God's existence, knowledge, wisdom, and power; knowing God is the ultimate aim of intellectual inquiry.
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r1.anchor: عاد ههنا إلى ذكر الدلائل الدالة على وجود الصانع

RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، والضحاك، ومقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, and Muqatil interpret 'splitter of grain and date-stone' as creator of them.
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r2.anchor: وهو مروي عن ابن عباس وقول الضحاك ومقاتل

RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r3.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r3.claim: Al-Wahidi says they use faliq in the sense of fatir, which Razi treats as compatible with the root sense of splitting.
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r3.anchor: قال الواحدي : ذهبوا بفالق مذهب فاطر

RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r4.claim: Razi explains creation from nothing as a figurative splitting of imagined, unbroken darkness: bringing something into existence can thus be called faliq, its originator.
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r4.anchor: فالشيء قبل أن دخل في الوجود كان معدوما محضا ونفيا صرفا

RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r5.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r5.claim: Most commentators take faliq literally as splitter: al-habb is a grain such as wheat or barley, and al-nawa is the stone inside fruit such as peach or date.

RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r6.claim: Once a seed or pit lies in moist earth, it splits above to send up a shoot and below to send roots into the earth, joining the two growths.
RAZI-FULL:v13p73#2/r6.anchor: إذا وقعت الحبة أو النواة في الأرض الرطبة

RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r1.claim: A seed's opposed upward shoot and downward root cannot arise from one natural tendency; their production points to divine creation and origination.
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r1.anchor: علمنا أن ذلك ليس بمقتضى الطبع والخاصية

RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r2.claim: Delicate root tips penetrate hard, dense soil despite being so fragile that slight finger pressure would turn them to liquid; their strength is divinely apportioned.
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r2.anchor: فحصول هذه القوى الشديدة لهذه الأجرام الضعيفة التي هي في غاية اللطافة لا بد وأن يكون بتقدير العزيز الحكيم

RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r3.claim: A single tree yields structures with different substances and properties, including layered walnut husks, shells, membranes, dense kernel, and oil; such diversity under uniform natural causes indicates a wise, willing creator.
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r3.anchor: فتولد هذه الأجسام المختلفة في طبائعها وصفاتها وألوانها وأشكالها وطعومها مع تساوي تأثيرات الطبائع والنجوم

RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r4.claim: One seed yields opposing qualities within a citron or grape: for example, citron peel is hot and dry while its flesh is cold and moist, evidencing a voluntary agent.
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r4.anchor: فتولد هذه الطبائع المضادة والخواص المتنافرة عن الحبة الواحدة لا بد وأن يكون بإيجاد الفاعل المختار

RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r5.claim: Fruits differ in whether edible flesh or a hard shell is inside or outside, in seed shapes and uses, and in whether they nourish one animal or poison another; their variety points beyond uniform nature and celestial influences to a wise creator.
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r5.anchor: اختلاف هذه الصفات والأشكال والأحوال مع اتحاد الطبائع وتأثيرات الكواكب يدل على أن كلها إنما حصلت بتخليق الفاعل المختار

RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r6.claim: A leaf's branching, ever finer veins let its attractive powers draw tiny earthly particles through narrow channels; this care in one leaf implies still greater providence in a tree and all plants.
RAZI-FULL:v13p74/r6.anchor: والخالق تعالى إنما فعل ذلك حتى أن القوى الجاذبة المركوزة في جرم تلك الورقة تقوى على جذب الأجزاء اللطيفة الأرضية

RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r1.claim: Plants serve animals, animals serve humans, and plants and animals feed or treat the human body; the final purpose of creating humans is knowledge, love, and worship of God.
RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r1.anchor: المقصود من تخليق الإنسان هو المعرفة والمحبة والخدمة

RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r2.claim: Contemplating the detailed veins of a single leaf leads toward knowledge of God's immeasurable favors and unending spiritual insight.
RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r2.anchor: واعرف كيفية خلقة تلك العروق والأوتار فيها

RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r3.claim: Strictly, al-hayy is what possesses life and al-mayyit what lacks it; on this definition, a plant is not living.
RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r3.anchor: أن { الحى } اسم لما يكون موصوفا بالحياة

RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the terms literally: a living human comes from dead semen and dead semen from a living human; likewise a chick comes from an egg and a dead egg from a chicken, showing opposites require a wise determiner.
RAZI-FULL:v13p75/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يخرج من النطفة بشرا حيا

RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r1.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes the terms figuratively: fresh, green growth emerges from dry grain, while dry grain comes from living, growing plants.
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج : يخرج النبات الغض الطري الخضر

RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also interprets the phrase figuratively: God brings believers from unbelievers, as Abraham, and unbelievers from believers, as Noah's son, as well as sinners from obedient people and vice versa.
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يخرج المؤمن من الكافر

RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r3.claim: An apparent harm can produce great benefit: a man given opium to kill him was saved when a snakebite counteracted the drug; such reversals, and their converse, show wise governance rather than a purposeless world.
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r3.anchor: ذكروا في الطب أن إنسانا سقوه الأفيون الكثير في الشراب لأجل أن يموت

RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r4.claim: The varied and counteracting outcomes in these examples show that the world has a wise governor who does not neglect creatures' interests or leave them purposeless.
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r4.anchor: وكل هذه الأحوال المختلفة والأفعال المتدافعة تدل على أن لهذا العالم مدبرا حكيما ما أهمل مصالح الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r5.speaker: نافع، وحمزة، والكسائي، وحفص عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r5.claim: Nafi, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Hafs from Asim geminate al-mayyit in both occurrences; the other readers lighten both, as with this form throughout the Quran.
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r5.anchor: قرأ نافع وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم

RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r6.claim: The noun phrase 'bringing the dead from the living' coordinates with 'splitter of grain and pit'; the preceding verb phrase explains that splitting, since sprouting is like bringing life from death.
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r6.anchor: معطوف على قوله : { فالق الحب والنوى }

RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r7.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r7.claim: Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani says the verb form conveys God's renewed provision moment by moment, while a participle suggests persistence in one state, as in the two cited examples.
RAZI-FULL:v13p76/r7.anchor: وضرب الشيخ عبد القاهر الجرجاني لهذا مثلا في كتاب

RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r1.claim: Since life is nobler than death, the more attentive verb form marks bringing the living from the dead, while the noun form marks the less emphasized reverse process.
RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r1.anchor: فوجب أن يكون الاعتناء بإخراج الحي من الميت أكثر من الاعتناء

RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r2.claim: One interpretation names God as creator, governor, benefactor, harm-giver, life-giver, and death-giver, then rebukes turning to idols.
RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم معناه : ذلكم الله المدبر

RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r3.claim: Another reading rebukes denial of resurrection: if God brought a living body once from dead semen, producing life again from dead dust is no less possible; if death can follow life, life can follow death.
RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r3.anchor: والثاني : أن المراد أنكم لما شاهدتم

RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r4.speaker: الصاحب بن عباد
RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r4.claim: Al-Sahib ibn Abbad argues that if God creates human deviation, it makes little sense to ask how people are turned away.

RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r5.claim: Razi replies that an uncaused preference between equal powers is mere chance and cannot ground blame; if a divine motive determines the choice, that motive is from God, restoring the opponent's own objection.
RAZI-FULL:v13p77/r5.anchor: فإن ترجح أحد الطرفين على الآخر لا لمرجح

STUDYQURAN:6:95/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r1.claim: Splitting grain and fruit stones brings life from what appears dead, linking the cleavage to God bringing the living from the dead.
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r1.anchor: That God is the Cleaver of the grain and the fruit stone is connected to His bringing forth the living from the dead

STUDYQURAN:6:95/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r2.claim: The semantic link between splitting and creation also appears in al-Fāṭir, “Originator,” whose root means “to split.”
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r2.anchor: The connection between “cleaving” or “splitting” and creating is also made semantically in the Divine Name al-Fāṭir, “the Originator,” which is derived from the root meaning “to split”

STUDYQURAN:6:95/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r3.claim: Bringing the living from the dead refers to first human creation and resurrection after death.
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r3.anchor: He brings forth the living from the dead both when He creates human beings the first time and when He brings them forth through resurrection after death

STUDYQURAN:6:95/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r4.claim: Bringing the dead from the living refers to God causing death, the end of earthly life.
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r4.anchor: He brings forth the dead from the living when He causes death, or the end of their earthly existence

STUDYQURAN:6:95/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r5.claim: The cycle evokes Muḥyī, Giver of Life, and Mumīt, Bringer of Death.
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r5.anchor: it is important to recall the two Divine Names Muḥyī (Giver of Life; 30:50; 41:39) and Mumīt (Bringer of Death)

STUDYQURAN:6:95/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r6.claim: The life-death cycles mean mabdaʾ (origin) and maʿād (return), transporting souls and all beings between this world and the next.
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r6.anchor: the complementary movements of creation and resurrection, referred to in Islamic discourse as mabdaʾ (origin) and maʿād (return)

STUDYQURAN:6:95/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r7.claim: Created nature likewise cycles through life and death: a dead seed emerges from a living plant and a living plant from a dead seed.
STUDYQURAN:6:95/r7.anchor: An analogous cycle of death and life is also seen in various ways in the created order

TAB-FULL:v9p420/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r1.claim: This reminds idolaters of God's proof against associating idols with Him: God alone deserves worship, as He is the one who splits seed and pits and brings forth plants and trees.
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r1.anchor: إن الذي له العبادة أيها الناس دون كل ما تعبدون

TAB-FULL:v9p420/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r2.claim: Faliq means splitting open grain from plants and pits from things that are planted, bringing forth crops and trees.
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r2.anchor: هو الله الذي فلق الحب، يعني: شق الحب من كل ما ينبت من النبات، فأخرج منه الزرع والنوى

TAB-FULL:v9p420/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r3.claim: Al-ḥabb is the plural of ḥabbah, and al-nawā is the plural of nawāh.
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r3.anchor: والحب جمع حبة، والنوى: جمع النواة

TAB-FULL:v9p420/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says God splits grain to produce an ear and a pit to produce a date palm.
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r4.anchor: عن السدي: {إن الله فالق الحب والنوى} [الأنعام: 95] ، أما فالق الحب والنوى: ففالق الحب عن السنبلة

TAB-FULL:v9p420/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r5.claim: Qatada says God splits grain and pits to bring forth plants.
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r5.anchor: عن قتادة: {فالق الحب والنوى} [الأنعام: 95] قال: «يفلق الحب والنوى عن النبات»

TAB-FULL:v9p420/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says God splits a pit to produce a palm and grain to produce its plants.
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فالق الحب والنوى} [الأنعام: 95] ، قال: «الله فالق ذلك، فلقه فأنبت منه ما أنبت

TAB-FULL:v9p420/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r7.speaker: الضحاك، ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak and Ibn Abbas are reported to interpret faliq as creator of grain and pits.
TAB-FULL:v9p420/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: {إن الله فالق الحب والنوى} [الأنعام: 95] قال: «خالق الحب والنوى»

TAB-FULL:v9p422/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p422/r1.speaker: أبو مالك، مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p422/r1.claim: Abu Malik and Mujahid describe faliq as the cleft found in a kernel and a grain.
TAB-FULL:v9p422/r1.anchor: عن أبي مالك، في قول الله: {إن الله فالق الحب والنوى} [الأنعام: 95] قال: «الشق الذي يكون في النواة وفي الحنطة»

TAB-FULL:v9p422/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p422/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v9p422/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak explains faliq as the creator of grain and pits, meaning each seed.
TAB-FULL:v9p422/r2.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {فالق الحب والنوى} [الأنعام: 95] يقول: " خالق الحب والنوى، يعني: كل حبة "

TAB-FULL:v9p422/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p422/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p422/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers splitting grain into plants and pits into trees, since the following statement about bringing the living from the dead and the dead from the living supports this sense.
TAB-FULL:v9p422/r3.anchor: وذلك أن الله جل ثناؤه أتبع ذلك بإخباره عن إخراجه الحي من الميت، والميت من الحي

TAB-FULL:v9p422/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p422/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p422/r4.claim: He rejects taking faliq simply to mean creator unless it means creating plants by splitting seed, since Arabic does not use falaqa for creating.
TAB-FULL:v9p422/r4.anchor: لا أعرف له وجها، لأنه لا يعرف في كلام العرب فلق الله الشيء بمعنى: خلق

TAB-FULL:v9p423/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r1.claim: God brings living ears from dead grain and living trees from dead pits, and reverses each cycle by producing grain and pits from living plants.
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r1.anchor: عن السدي: أما: {يخرج الحي من الميت} [الأنعام: 95] ، «فيخرج السنبلة الحية من الحبة الميتة

TAB-FULL:v9p423/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r2.claim: In Arab usage, a rooted tree or stalk still growing is called living; when dry, withered, or cut at its root it is called dead.
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r2.anchor: فإذا يبس وجف أو قطع من أصله سموه ميتا

TAB-FULL:v9p423/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r3.claim: Al-Suddī gives reciprocal examples of a live ear from a dead kernel, a kernel from an ear, a palm from a pit, and a pit from a palm.
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r3.anchor: عن السدي: أما: {يخرج الحي من الميت} [الأنعام: 95] ، «فيخرج السنبلة الحية من الحبة الميتة

TAB-FULL:v9p423/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r4.speaker: أبو مالك
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r4.claim: Abū Mālik likewise explains the phrase through palms and pits, and grain and ears in both directions.
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r4.anchor: عن أبي مالك: {يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي} [الأنعام: 95] قال: «النخلة من النواة

TAB-FULL:v9p423/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās applies it to apparently dead sperm emitted from a living person, from which a living human is then produced.
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس: قوله: {إن الله فالق الحب والنوى يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي} [الأنعام: 95] قال: «يخرج النطفة الميتة

TAB-FULL:v9p423/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the grain-and-pit reading because it directly follows the mention of splitting grain and pits.
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r6.anchor: لأنه عقيب قوله: {إن الله فالق الحب والنوى} [الأنعام: 95]

TAB-FULL:v9p423/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r7.claim: The general wording also includes Ibn ʿAbbās's example: God brings every dead thing from a living body and every living thing from a dead body.
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r7.anchor: فإنه داخل في عمومه ما روي عن ابن عباس في تأويل ذلك

TAB-FULL:v9p423/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r8.claim: God alone is the agent of all these acts of creation.
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r8.anchor: فاعل ذلك كله الله جل جلاله

TAB-FULL:v9p423/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r9.claim: The rebuke asks why people turn from truth and urges reflection: the giver of crops and fruits should not have powerless, deaf, blind partners in worship.
TAB-FULL:v9p423/r9.anchor: أفلا تتدبرون فتعلمون أنه لا ينبغي أن يجعل لمن أنعم عليكم بفلق الحب والنوى

SULAMI:v1p209#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p209#5/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p209#5/r1.claim: God brings forth what is in the heart's seed: sincerity and ostentation.
SULAMI:v1p209#5/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : مظهر ما في حبة القلب من الإخلاص والرياء

TABRISI:6:95-96/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:95-96/r4.claim: Falq means splitting; it can also name a low place in the earth, as if split from it.
TABRISI:6:95-96/r4.anchor: اللغة: الفلق الشق يقال فلقه الصبح لأن الظلام ينفلق عنه والفلق المطمئن من الأرض

TABRISI:6:95-96/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:95-96/r5.claim: Ḥabb is the plural of ḥabba and includes grains without pits, such as wheat and barley; nawā is the plural of nawāt.
TABRISI:6:95-96/r5.anchor: والحب جمع حبة جمع حبة وهو كل ما لا يكون له نوى كالبر والشعير والنوى جمع نواة

TABRISI:6:95-96/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:95-96/r11.claim: The discourse returns to arguing with polytheists through wonders of creation and subtle governance.
TABRISI:6:95-96/r11.anchor: ثم عاد الكلام إلى الاحتجاج على المشركين بعجائب الصنع ولطائف التدبير

TABRISI:6:95-96/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96/r12.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والسدي
TABRISI:6:95-96/r12.claim: Al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Suddi say God splits dry, dead grain to make plants and dry pits to make palms and trees.
TABRISI:6:95-96/r12.anchor: أي شاق الحبة اليابسة الميتة فيخرج منها النبات وشاق النواة اليابسة فيخرج منها النخل والشجر عن الحسن وقتادة والسدي

TABRISI:6:95-96/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96/r13.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
TABRISI:6:95-96/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Dahhak alternatively gloss this as God creating, originating, and bringing grain and pits into being.
TABRISI:6:95-96/r13.anchor: وقيل: معناه خالق الحب والنوى ومنشئهما ومبدئهما عن ابن عباس والضحاك

TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد وأبو مالك
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r1.claim: Mujahid and Abu Malik say the phrase refers to the cleft in grain and pits, an evident marvel of God’s power.
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r1.anchor: في استوائه عن مجاهد وأبي مالك

TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the living as green, tender plants emerging from dry grain and dry grain emerging from living, growing plants; Arabs call a green upright tree alive and a dry, cut, or uprooted tree dead.
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r2.anchor: أي يخرج النبات الغض الطري الخضر من الحب اليابس ويخرج الحب اليابس من النبات الحي النامي عن الزجاج

TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan, Qatada, Ibn Zayd, and others say God creates a living person from dead semen and dead semen from a living person; al-Tabrisi calls this the soundest view.
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: معناه يخلق الحي من النطفة وهي موات ويخلق النطفة وهي موات من الحي عن الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد

TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r4.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r4.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi says the phrase means that God brings birds from eggs and eggs from birds.
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: معناه يخرج الطير من البيض والبيض من الطير عن الجبائي

TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r5.claim: Another reported interpretation takes it to mean that God brings a believer from an unbeliever and an unbeliever from a believer.
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: معناه يخرج المؤمن من الكافر والكافر من المؤمن

TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r6.claim: God is the one who performs all the acts just described.
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r6.anchor: { ذلكم الله } أي فاعل ذلك كله الله

TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r7.claim: The phrase asks how people can be turned from truth and diverted by manifest proofs toward falsehood; reflection shows they should not associate a partner in worship with their benefactor.
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r7.anchor: { فأنى تؤفكون } أي تصرفون عن الحق ويذهب بكم عن هذه الأدلة الظاهرة إلى الباطل

THALABI:v4p171#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p171#2/r1.claim: God splits grain from its plant and the date stone from its tree, bringing crops and trees out of them.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r1.anchor: فالق الحب أي فلق الحب عن النبات، ومخرج منها الزرع وشاق النوى

THALABI:v4p171#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v4p171#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says the phrase means the two clefts intended by the wording.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يعني الشقين الذين عناهما.

THALABI:v4p171#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v4p171#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak defines habb as seed without a pit and nawā as the pits of fruits.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك: فالق الحب والنوى، الحب جمع الحبة وهي كل ما لم يكن لها نواة

THALABI:v4p171#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p171#2/r4.claim: The alternation of living and dead things demonstrates that God alone is the source of creation; those turning away are turned from truth.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r4.anchor: يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي ذلكم الله فأنى تؤفكون تصدون عن الحق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r1.claim: In the report of Ata, Ibn Abbas glosses the splitting of grain and pits as the production of plants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (يريد: بالنبات)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi distinguishes grain without a pit, such as wheat and barley, from pits without grain, such as date and peach stones; God splits both into growth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: (الحب ما لم يكن له نوى كالبر والشعير، والنوى: ما لم يكن له حب مثل نوى التمر والخوخ وغيرهما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والسدي وابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r3.claim: They explain the splitting as a grain opening into an ear and a date pit opening into a palm.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن (¬5) وقتادة (¬6) والسدي (¬7) وابن زيد (¬8): (فلق الحبة عن السنبلة والنواة عن النخلة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq says God splits dry grain and dry pits to bring green leaves out of them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (أي: يشق الحبة اليابسة والنواة اليابسة فيخرج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r5.speaker: مجاهد وأبو مالك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r5.claim: Mujahid and Abu Malik take fāliq to refer to the clefts or splits within the grain and pit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد (¬2) وأبو مالك: (يعني: الشقين الذين فيهما)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r6.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r6.claim: They take fāliq to mean creator, treating it as equivalent to fāṭir; this view is also transmitted from Ibn Abbas.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r6.anchor: وهو قول الضحاك ومقاتل: {فالق الحب والنوى} (أي: خالقهما)، ذهبوا بفالق مذهب فاطر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r7.claim: Muqatil includes all grains and all fruits with pits, naming wheat, barley, corn, dates, peaches, figs, and other fruits.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r7.anchor: قال مقاتل: (يعني: خالق الحب البر والشعير والذرة والحبوب كلها، {والنوى} يعني: نوى كل ثمرة لها نوى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r8.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r8.claim: Al-Layth says nawā is the pit of dates and similar fruit; nawāt is the singular, and the verb can mean that a date's pit has formed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p301/r8.anchor: قال الليث (¬8): (النوى: نوى التمر وأشباهه من كل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r1.claim: They explain living from dead and dead from living as a human or offspring emerging from sperm or egg, then sperm and egg coming from the living.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يخرج من النطفة بشرا حيا ثم يخرج النطفة الميتة من الحي)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r2.claim: In Ata's report, Ibn Abbas and Hasan take this as a believer coming from an unbeliever and vice versa, or a disobedient person from an obedient one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (يخرج المؤمن من الكافر، والكافر من المؤمن، والعاصي من الطائع)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r3.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the living is brought out of the dead as a plant from a seed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq chooses the plant reading: tender green growth comes from dry grain, and dry grain comes from living, growing plants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r4.anchor: وهذا اختيار أبي إسحاق قال: معنى {يخرج الحي من الميت} يخرج النبات: الغض الطري الخضر من الحب اليابس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God alone, without partner, performs these acts, and asks how people can deny this.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1): (يريد: الله وحده لا شريك له يفعل هذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says visible creation rebuts their denial of resurrection: the one who created these things can resurrect them, so how are they turned from truth after the proof?
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p303/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج: (احتج الله عليهم بما يشاهدونه من خلقه؛ لأنهم أنكروا البعث، فأعلمهم أنه خلق هذه الأشياء

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r1.claim: His rendering describes God as splitting grains and kernels, bringing life from death and death from life, splitting dawn, making night a resting place, and setting the sun and moon for reckoning.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r1.anchor: Allah o dâneleri, çekirdekleri pörtleten, ölüden diri çıkarır ve diriden ölü çıkaran

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r3.claim: Falq is splitting or cracking; habb is a collective noun for grain, and nawā for kernels, with the former pointing to herb seeds and the latter to tree seeds.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r3.anchor: “Falk”, şakk etmek, çatlatmaktır. “Habb”, habbenin, “nevâ” da çekirdek demek olan “nevât”ın cem‘i makamında ism-i cinstir.

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r4.claim: Because both are plants, he finds it more apt to see nawā as the plant germ inside a grain, analogous to the kernel within a date or grape.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r4.anchor: ot ve ağaç ikisi de nebâtî olduğundan “nevât”ı dânenin içindeki mâye-i nebâtî gibi mülâhaza etmek mânen daha muvâfık olacaktır

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r5.claim: He notes nüveyye as a diminutive of nevât and suggests that the French word noyau appears to derive from it.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r5.anchor: “nevât”ın tasgīri olarak “nüveyye” dahi denilir ki, Fransızların “noyau”

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r6.claim: A seed develops inner motion and pressure that split it, turning rest into motion and continuity into separation; a shoot rises through the upper crack while roots descend through the lower one.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r6.anchor: Allah o dâne, o çekirdek dâhilinden bir hareket, bir tazyik, bir intac husûle getirir; onu altından üstünden falk eder, çatlatır

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r7.claim: The fine rootlets can split hard ground and even stone, illustrating the diverse and wondrous powers operating within plants as signs of the Creator’s power.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r7.anchor: sert çuvaldızların, sivri bıçakların nüfuz edemeyeceği derecede sulb olan yerleri ve bazı zaman kaskatı taşları bile çatlatır

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r8.claim: He urges readers who want fuller appreciation of this intricacy to study plant anatomy, tissues, and vegetative instincts.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r8.anchor: nebâtâtın teşrîhini, ensâcını, garâiz-i uvziyesini tedkik ve mütalaa etsinler.

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r9.claim: The varied structures and traits work together to yield fruit; each mature fruit breaks away and returns to the soil with many seeds for a new generation.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r9.anchor: maksûd-ı aslî olan semere tevellüd eder. Bir habbe veya bir çekirdek yerine kat kat kutular, mahfazalar içinde yüzlercesi meydana gelir.

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r10.claim: The same origin and equal natural conditions still produce diverse forms and traits, proving wise, merciful, freely acting divine governance rather than nature or elements.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r10.anchor: Menşe’ bir ve tabiatın, nücûmun, fusûlün, anâsırın tesirleri şerâiti müsâvî olduğu hâlde bir habbeden, bir çekirdekten bu kadar muhtelif ecsâm

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r11.claim: The power that grows plants from seeds also creates seeds from plants; God brings life from death and death from life, a pattern even more evident and extensive in animals.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r11.anchor: Gerek dâneyi, çekirdeği şaktan nebat ve eşcâr çıkarmak ve gerek bir şaktan dâne, çekirdek halk etmek her iki mânasıyla فَالِقُ ٱلْحَبِّ وَٱلنَّوَىٰ O’dur.

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r12.claim: The question asks how people can turn to worship others or escape God’s rule; no state, whether life or death, plant or animal, earth or sky, darkness or light, lies beyond him.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r12.anchor: O’ndan nasıl çevrilir de başkalarına taparsınız?

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r13.claim: After establishing that none escapes God’s power, Elmalılı points to his splitting darkness to bring dawn as further evidence of that power.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r13.anchor: Gerek hayatta olun gerek mematta, gerek hayvanlara karışın gerek otlara, gerek yere geçin gerek göğe çıkın

ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r7.claim: The same principle unfolds the splitting of grain and seeds, the sequence of purification and development, and rejects treating the elements as an effective first cause.
ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r7.anchor: aynı düstur dâhilinde فَالِقُ ٱلْحَبِّ وَٱلنَّوَىٰ mazmununu teşrih ve silsile-i ıstıfâ ve tekâmülü tavzih

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:95/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:95/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:95/r1.claim: These recurring acts of creation are miracles and signs of divine power, though familiarity often keeps people from appreciating them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:95/r1.anchor: her biri başlı başına birer mûcize olan, fakat her zaman tekrarlandığı için insanların önemini kavramaktan gafil olduğu başlıca yaratılış olaylarına ve ilâhî kudretin işaretlerine dikkat çekilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:95/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:95/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:95/r2.claim: God splits seeds and pits to bring forth plants, and brings the dead from the living and the living from the dead; these transformations expose human turning away from the Creator and worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:95/r2.anchor: böylece O, ölüden diriyi, diriden ölüyü, tohumdan ve çekirdekten bitkileri, bitkiden tohum ve çekirdekleri çıkarmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:95/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:95/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:95/r3.claim: The verse asks how people can turn from the truth and refuse to recognize God as Creator and worship him despite such repeated signs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:95/r3.anchor: insanoğlunun nasıl olup da gerçeğe sırtını dönebildiği, O’nu yaratıcı olarak tanıyıp kulluk etmekten geri durabildiği sorulmaktadır.

BURHAN:v4p110/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p110/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p110/r1.claim: Zarkashī endorses al-Zamakhsharī: ومخرج الميت coordinates with فالق الحب والنوى, not يخرج, because it is not an explanation of فالق الحب.
BURHAN:v4p110/r1.anchor: والتحقيق ما قاله الزمخشري انه عطف على

BURHAN:v4p110/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p110/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p110/r2.claim: Coordination on the wording follows an overt grammatical governor on the first coordinated term; this is the basic kind, illustrated by two predicates governed by ليس.
BURHAN:v4p110/r2.anchor: فالاول إن يكون باعتبار عمل موجود في المعطوف عليه فهو العطف على اللفظ نحو ليس زيد بقائم ولا ذاهب

BURHAN:v4p110/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p110/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p110/r3.claim: Coordination on syntactic position applies a case that is not overt on the first term but is implied by its governor, as in an accusative predicate after an underlying ليس.
BURHAN:v4p110/r3.anchor: والثاني إن يكون باعتبار عمل لم يوجد في المعطوف إلا أنه مقدر الوجود لوجود طالبه فهو العطف على الموضع

BURHAN:v4p110/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p110/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p110/r8.claim: Coordination by supposition applies a case whose governor and overt case are both absent, but are imagined from a common construction, such as الجر after ليس as though باء were present.
BURHAN:v4p110/r8.anchor: والثالث إن يكون باعتبار عمل لم يوجد هو ولا طالبه هو العطف على التوهم نحو ليس زيد قائما ولا ذاهب بجر ذاهب

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r1.claim: Umayya says a gift adorns its recipient only when it brings good, while Abu Tammam depicts gifts as honor and says the act of asking can itself yield distinction.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r1.anchor: وما كل العطاء يزين ! ) مع قول أبي تمام ، + البسيط + : ( تدعى عطاياه وفرا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r2.claim: Jarir portrays friends as arrows shot by enemies, and Abu Nuwas says a wise person discovers an enemy hidden in the world's guise of a friend.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r2.anchor: بعثن الهوى ثم ارتمين قلوبنا بأسهم أعداء وهن صديق

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r3.claim: Kathir refuses separation from his beloved and names al-Hajibiyya as first; Abu Tammam generalizes that love remains for the first beloved wherever the heart goes.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r3.anchor: أبينا وقلنا : الحاجبية أول ) مع قول أبي تمام

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r4.claim: The author juxtaposes al-Mutanabbi's question about loyalty to Shabib's companion with Abu Tammam's claim that treachery is not unique to Hind but belongs to every beautiful woman.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r4.anchor: وعند من اليوم الوفاء لصاحب شبيب وأوفى من ترى أخوان

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r5.claim: Al-Buhturi contrasts a silted stream with the Nile at flood, while al-Mutanabbi says one aiming for the sea considers small streams insignificant.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r5.anchor: فحاولت ورد النيل عند احتفاله ) مع قول المتنبي

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r6.claim: Al-Mutanabbi says generosity is innate in his subjects, excused by neither youth nor age; al-Buhturi likewise says generosity begins with them as their lives begin.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r6.anchor: كأنما يولد الندى معهم لا صغر عاذر ولا هرم ) مع قول البحتري

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r7.claim: Al-Buhturi says the hand, rather than the sword, delivers the cut; al-Mutanabbi depicts his sword-bearing hand as ending the equality between swords.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r7.anchor: فإن الكف ، لا السيف ، تقطع ) مع قول المتنبي

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r8.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r8.claim: Al-Buhturi says jealous rivals praise him despite lacking generosity, then answers with his own liberality; Abu Tammam evokes generosity's former paths and traces having disappeared.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p355/r8.anchor: ساموك من حسد فأفضل منهم غير الجواد وجاد غير المفضل

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r6.claim: Because 6:94 denies independent causes and false divine partners, the next passage explains that those causes are God's managed creations and act only by His measure.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r6.anchor: لما انتهى الكلام في الآية السابقة إلى نفي استقلال الأسباب في تأثيرها، وبطلان كون أربابهم شفعاء من دون الله

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r7.claim: Al-falaq means splitting: God cleaves grain and date stones, from which the plants and trees that feed people grow.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r7.anchor: الفلق هو الشق. لما انتهى الكلام في الآية السابقة إلى نفي استقلال الأسباب في تأثيرها

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r8.claim: God alone brings vegetation from grain and seed; these created causes serve human life only through His management and measure.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r8.anchor: فالله سبحانه هو يشق الحب والنوى فينبت منهما النبات والشجر اللذين يرتزق الناس من حبه وثمره

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r9.claim: God brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī refers back to his discussion of this at 3:27.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r9.anchor: وهو يخرج الحي من الميت والميت من الحي - وقد مر تفسير ذلك في الكلام على الآية 27 من سورة آل عمران

TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r1.claim: The Qur'an treats the effects of created things as genuinely attributable to them, and likewise attributes human actions and conditions to people.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r1.anchor: الأشياء الواقعة في دار الوجود كالسماء وكواكبها ونجومها والأرض وجبالها ووهادها وسهلها وبحرها وبرها وعناصرها

TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r2.claim: The Qur'an distinguishes chosen human acts, for which people may be held accountable, from conditions such as illness or aging that are not chosen.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r2.anchor: فنعتقد أن له أفعالا وآثارا منسوبة إليه نؤاخذه في بعض أفعاله التي ترجع بنحو إلى اختياره كالأكل والشرب والمشي

TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r3.claim: The Qur'an affirms general causality: every contingent thing exists through another, an effect cannot exist without its cause, and the complete cause entails its effect.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r3.anchor: وهو أن كل ما يجوز له في نفسه أن يوجد وأن لا يوجد فهو إنما يوجد عن غيره

TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r4.claim: Qur'anic arguments for God's attributes and for later events presuppose causal regularity; if effects could fail despite complete causes, those arguments would fail.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#3/r4.anchor: وقد أنفذه الله سبحانه في كلامه في موارد كثيرة استدل فيها من طريق ما له من الصفات العليا على ثبوت آثارها ومعاليلها

TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r1.claim: The Qur'an's inferences from conditions to outcomes assume that effects follow when necessary conditions are present and impediments absent.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r1.anchor: ولو جاز أن يتخلف أثر من مؤثره إذا اجتمعت الشرائط اللازمة وارتفعت الموانع المنافية لم يصح شيء من هذه الحجج والأدلة البتة

TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r2.claim: God's creation extends to everything in the cosmos; Qur'anic passages also assign the things' characteristics, actions, transformations, and goals to divine determination and guidance.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r2.anchor: إنا نجد أن الله سبحانه في كلامه يعمم خلقه على كل ما يصدق عليه شيء من أجزاء الكون

TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r3.claim: Created things receive their limits, changing states, actions, and ends through God's determination and guidance, which directs each kind toward its goal.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r3.anchor: وفي هذه الآيات نوع آخر من البيان أخذت فيه الأشياء منسوبة إلى الخلقة وأعمالها وأنواع آثارها وحركاتها وسكناتها منسوبة إلى التقدير والهداية الإلهية

TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r4.claim: The interconnected, harmonized cosmos operates under one system with no governor but God, an argument for the unity of divine governance.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#4/r4.anchor: أن أجزاء الكون متصل بعضه ببعض متلائم بعض منه مع بعض متوحدة في الوجود يحكم فيها نظام واحد لا مدبر له إلا الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r1.speaker: جمع من الباحثين
TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r1.claim: Some researchers say morally ugly acts cannot be attributed to God, so human acts must be created by humans; otherwise choice, commands, and accountability would collapse. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this reasoning.

TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r2.claim: The argument confuses real existence with conventional and social categories, which people form to organize communal life and pursue its welfare.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r2.anchor: وقد ذهب على هؤلاء في بحثهم أن يفرقوا بين الأمور الحقيقية التي تنال الوجود والتحقق حقيقة، والأمور الاعتبارية

TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r3.claim: Everything other than God that counts as a thing is created, and everything created is good in its actual existence; creation and goodness therefore coincide ontologically.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r3.anchor: وأن كل مخلوق فهو متصف بالحسن

TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r4.claim: Evil and sin are relational or conventional descriptions rather than features of a thing's created reality; adultery and marriage are materially similar acts distinguished by law and social consequences.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#5/r4.anchor: مثاله الزنا والنكاح وهما فعلان متماثلان لا يختلفان في حقيقتهما ووجودهما النوعي مثلا

TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r1.claim: An act such as injustice is, in the created order, a set of motions and effects; its blameworthy title belongs to its social or legal setting.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r1.anchor: وأما بحسب التكوين فليس إلا أثرا أو مجموع آثار من قبيل الحركات العارضة للإنسان

TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r2.claim: Creation applies to external reality, not to moral labels, obedience, social rank, or other conventional descriptions that arise through legislation or social judgment.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r2.anchor: وأما ما وراء ذلك من جهات القبح والحسن والمعصية والطاعة وسائر الأوصاف والعناوين الاجتماعية الطارئة

TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r3.claim: Since moral and legal evaluation belongs to a different domain from creation, universal creation does not abolish commands, prohibitions, reward, or punishment.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r3.anchor: ظهر أن عموم الخلقة لكل شيء لا يستلزم شيئا من المفاسد التي ذكروها كبطلان نظام الأمر والنهي

TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r4.claim: A dualist account conflicts with the Qur'an's teaching that God alone creates, governs, guides, owns, and encompasses everything.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r4.anchor: وكيف يسوغ لمن تدبر كلامه تعالى أن يفتي بمثل هذه الثنوية وكلامه مشحون بأنه خالق كل شيء

TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r5.claim: A second objection infers occasionalism from God's universal creation: only God affects things, and fire merely precedes heat by divine habit, without a real causal bond.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#6/r5.anchor: وإنما هي عادته تعالى جرت أن يخلق ما نسميه معلولا عقيب ما نسميه علة من غير أن تكون بينهما رابطة

TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r1.claim: Occasionalism destroys the rational causal law used to establish the Creator and to validate scripture, making its own argument self-defeating.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r1.anchor: وهذا النظر يبطل قانون العلية والمعلولية العام الذي عليه المدار في القضاء العقلي

TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r2.claim: The objection confuses causes at the same level with causes in a hierarchy; two complete causes cannot independently converge on one effect, but a higher cause can cause a lower one and its effect.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r2.anchor: هؤلاء إنما وقعوا فيما وقعوا من جهة خلطهم بين العلل الطولية والعرضية

TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r3.claim: More precisely, the error is conflating the source from which a thing comes into being with the means by which it comes about.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r3.anchor: منشأ الخطأ هو عدم التمييز بين الفاعل بمعنى ما منه والفاعل بمعنى ما به

TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r4.claim: Another view treats known proximate causes as excluding God, leaving Him responsible only for initial creation and assigning unexplained phenomena to hidden causes; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r4.anchor: حسبوا أن ما له علة ظاهرة معلومة من الأشياء فهي العلة له دونه تعالى وإلا لزم اجتماع علتين مستقلتين

TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r5.speaker: جم غفير من أهل الكلام
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r5.claim: Many theologians hold that a possible being needs God to originate it but not to sustain it; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this account of dependence.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r5.anchor: إنما يحتاج إلى الواجب في حدوثه لا في بقائه، وهو الذي يصر عليه جم غفير من أهل الكلام

TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r6.claim: He calls this an Israeli idea that entered Muslim scholarship and says it leads to denying badaʾ and abrogation; he judges it among the worst illusions.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#7/r6.anchor: رأي إسرائيلي تسرب في أذهان عدة من الباحثين من المسلمين ومن فروع ذلك قولهم باستحالة البداء والنسخ

TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r1.claim: The Qur'an counters the claim that God is needed only for origination by appealing to observable cosmic order and ongoing change as signs of God's existence and unity.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r1.anchor: فإن الله سبحانه يستدل على وجود الصانع ووحدته بالآيات المشهودة في العالم

TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r2.claim: The signs include celestial motions, seasonal change, rivers, rain, useful animals and plants, and the stages and transformations of human life.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r2.anchor: وهو النظام الجاري في كل نوع من الخليقة وما يجري عليه في مسير وجوده وأمد حياته من التغير والتحول والفعل والانفعال

TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r3.claim: These conditions and effects form an ongoing chain: each day's events cause the next day's events and depend on what preceded them; independent persistence would invalidate the Qur'anic proofs.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r3.anchor: وكل مجموع منها في حين علة للمجموع الحاصل بعد ذلك الحين، وحوادث اليوم علل حوادث الغد

TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r4.claim: Nothing in the world creates itself or is explained by a similar dependent thing; the causal chain must end in God, an existent whose being cannot lapse or change.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r4.anchor: فإن من الضروري أن شيئا من هذه الموجودات لم يفطر ذاته ولم يوجد نفسه

TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r5.claim: Divine bestowal is not a transfer that leaves its recipient self-sufficient: if a created thing became independently necessary, its dependence and possible destruction would contradict that claim.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#8/r5.anchor: إذ لو كانت إفاضة الوجود على هذه الوتيرة عاد الوجود المفاض مستقلا بنفسه واجبا بذاته

TABATABAI:6:91-105#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#9/r1.claim: All things belong to God and receive existence from Him continuously; when that influx ceases, they vanish. Their dependence thus extends from origination to persistence.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#9/r1.anchor: فالأشياء كما تستفيض منه تعالى الوجود في أول كونها وحدوثها كذلك تستفيض منه ذلك في حال بقائها

TABATABAI:6:91-105#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#9/r2.claim: The cosmos is an integrated order of mutual benefit: humans benefit from animals and plants, plants from earth and atmosphere, and earthly and celestial systems support each other toward each kind's fulfillment.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#9/r2.anchor: ينتفع فيها الإنسان مثلا بالنظام الجاري في الحيوان والنبات، والنبات مثلا بالنظام الجاري في الأرض والجو المحيط بها

TABATABAI:6:91-105#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#9/r3.claim: Divine determination includes creating each thing with defined capacities, assigning its actions and destination, and guiding it along the stages of its existence through causes.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#9/r3.anchor: وليس هذا التقدير والتدبير إلا عن فطر ذواتها وإيجاد هوياتها وصوغ أعيانها بضرب كل منها في قالب

TABATABAI:6:91-105#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#10/r1.claim: He rejects the picture of God creating things and then withdrawing while they run independently under natural laws, with God returning only to judge or occasionally intervene.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#10/r1.anchor: أن الله سبحانه خلق ذوات الأشياء على ما لها من الخصوصيات والشخصيات ثم اعتزلها وما كان يسعه إلا أن يعتزل

TABATABAI:6:91-105#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#10/r2.speaker: هؤلاء
TABATABAI:6:91-105#10/r2.claim: These thinkers say miracles occur by God's sole will through suspension of ordinary causal laws; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects that suspension as incompatible with general causality.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#10/r2.anchor: وهذا هو السر في إصرار هؤلاء على أن المعجزات وخوارق العادات ونحوهما إنما تتحقق بالإرادة الإلهية وحدها ونقض قانون العلية العام

TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r1.claim: In the clay tradition, the two portions are mixed: grain signifies believers’ clay, loved by God, while the kernel signifies disbelievers’ clay, which has distanced itself from good and truth.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r1.anchor: النوى طينة الكافرين الذين نأوا عن كل خير

TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r2.claim: The report identifies the living drawn from the dead as a believer emerging from disbelievers’ clay, and the dead drawn from the living as a disbeliever emerging from believers’ clay; mixing and later separation explain death and life.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r2.anchor: فالحي المؤمن الذي يخرج من طينة الكافر

TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī classifies the grain-and-kernel interpretation as inward rather than apparent meaning, notes that other reports give it too, and defers discussion of the clay traditions.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r3.anchor: الرواية من أخبار الطينة وسيجيء البحث فيها فيما يناسبه من المحل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r5.claim: God splits the grain to bring forth a plant and the date pit to produce a palm.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r5.anchor: { إن الله فالق الحب } شاقة بالنبات { والنوى } بالنخلة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r6.claim: God brings a living human from dead sperm and dead sperm from the living.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r6.anchor: { يخرج الحي من الميت } يخرج النطفة بشرا حيا { ومخرج الميت } النطفة { من الحي }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r7.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r7.claim: An alternative reported gloss is that God brings a believer from an unbeliever and an unbeliever from a believer.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r7.anchor: وقيل: يخرج المؤمن من الكافر، والكافر من المؤمن { ذلكم الله } الذي فعل هذه الأشياء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r8.claim: The God who performs these observable acts is their Lord; the question challenges how they turn from truth after clarification.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r8.anchor: { ذلكم الله } الذي فعل هذه الأشياء التي تشاهدونها ربكم { فأنى تؤفكون } فمن أين تصرفون عن الحق بعد البيان!

BURHAN:v1p130/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p130/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p130/r7.claim: The wording contrasts nominal مخرج الميت in al-Anʿām with the verbal يخرج form in the second parallel passage.
BURHAN:v1p130/r7.anchor: فى الأنعام ﴿ يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي ﴾ والثانى ﴿ يخرج ﴾ بالفعل

ITQAN:v3p34/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p34/r10.speaker: ابن الصائغ
ITQAN:v3p34/r10.claim: The third purpose is honor: examples put men before women, the free before the enslaved, the living before the dead, and hearing before sight. Ibn ʿAtiyya reports al-Naqqash’s argument that this ordering favors hearing and sight.
ITQAN:v3p34/r10.anchor: الثالث التشريف كتقديم الذكر على الأنثى نحو

ITQAN:v2p578#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p578#2/r5.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
ITQAN:v2p578#2/r5.claim: Fakhr al-Dīn says the more striking act, bringing living from dead, is expressed as an imperfect to signal renewal, as in 'God mocks them.'
ITQAN:v2p578#2/r5.anchor: قال الإمام فخر الدين لما كان الاعتناء بشأن إخراج الحي من الميت أشد أتى فيه بالمضارع ليدل على التجدد كما في قوله ﴿ الله يستهزئ بهم ﴾

NAHHAS:v2p82/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p82/r11.claim: God splits dead seeds and grain to produce green growth, then produces dead seeds from green growth, illustrating life from death and death from life.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r11.anchor: أي يشق النواة الميتة فيخرج منها ورقا أخضر وكذا الحبة

NAHHAS:v2p82/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v2p82/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the living human as coming from dead semen and semen as coming from a living human.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r12.anchor: وروى عن ابن عباس يخرج البشر الحي من النطفة الميتة

NAHHAS:v2p82/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p82/r13.claim: Given visible evidence of God’s power, the question asks how people can be turned away from truth.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r13.anchor: فمن أين تصرفون عن الحق مع ما ترون من قدرة الله

ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r5.claim: God splits dry grain and date stones to bring out fresh green growth; the dry seed then comes from the living plant.
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r5.anchor: أي يشق الحبة اليابسة الميتة والنواة اليابسة فيخرج منها ورقا أخضر.

ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r6.claim: The living from the dead is tender, fresh green vegetation emerging from dry grain; the dead from the living is dry grain from a growing plant.
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r6.anchor: أي يخرج النبات الغض الطري الخضر من الحب اليابس.

ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r7.claim: Observable creation answers deniers of resurrection: the One who created these things is able to resurrect them.
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r7.anchor: احتج الله جل ثناؤه عليهم بما يشاهدون من خلقه لأنهم أنكروا البعث

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f1.claim: A verb marks renewal and an active event, while a noun marks settled stability; the Qur'an also uses a participle for a future event treated as already certain.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f1.anchor: فخلاصة الأمر أن الفعل يدل على الحدث والتجدد والاسم يدل على الثبوت والاستقرار

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f5.claim: In 6:95, the living are paired with a verb for movement and renewal, while the dead are paired with a noun for stillness and stability.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f5.anchor: فاستعمل الفعل مع الحي فقال: (يخرج) واستعمل الاسم مع الميت فقال: (مخرج)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f7.claim: Unlike Al Imran's change-filled context, Al Anam presents God's attributes, power, and favor; its opening nouns and noun forms fit that setting, with a verb for living movement.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f7.anchor: في حين أن السياق في سورة الأنعام مختلف وليس السياق في التغييرات وإنما هو في صفات الله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r4.claim: After proving divine unity, prophethood, and the efficacy of God’s command, the passage turns the listener to ponder fresh signs, including the earlier proofs and Abraham’s argument, to know God’s essence and attributes.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r4.anchor: ولما ثبتت الوحدانية والنبوة والرسالة وتقاريع من تقاريعها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r5.claim: God splits seeds into crops and plants; emergence from nonexistence is figuratively a splitting of the imagined darkness of nothingness.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r5.anchor: وعبر بذلك لأن الشيء قبل وجوده كان معدوما

BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r6.claim: A kernel inside edible fruit is split to produce trees, though it is not itself the end sought; its subtle wisdoms point to the perfect, singular Creator.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r6.anchor: ولا يكون مقصودا لذاته بفلقها عن الأشجار

BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r7.speaker: الإمام الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r7.claim: Al-Rāzī’s account observes a seed splitting in moist soil and sending a shoot upward and roots downward.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r7.anchor: قال الإمام الرازي ما حاصله : إن النواة والحبة تكون

BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r8.speaker: الإمام الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī identifies the seed as the connecting cause joining the tree that rises above ground and the roots descending below.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r8.anchor: وتلك الحبة أو النواة سبب واصل بين الشجرتين

BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r1.speaker: الإمام الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r1.claim: A tiny seed develops into a tree with varied substances and successive branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit, demonstrating the power of the freely choosing Creator.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r1.anchor: إذا تأملت ظهور شجرة من نواة صغيرة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r2.speaker: الإمام الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r2.claim: Walnuts and almonds have four layers of covering around the intended kernel; the varied textures and products of one tree exceed what uniform natural causes explain.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r2.anchor: فتولد هذه الأجسام المختلفة طبعا وصفة ولونا وشكلا وطعما مع تساوي تأثيرات الطبائع

BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r3.speaker: الإمام الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r3.claim: Fruits combine contrasting qualities, and their useful parts occupy different positions: the edible core may be inside, outside, absent, or encompass the whole fruit; this variety indicates a choosing Creator.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r3.anchor: واختلاف هذه الطبائع والأحوال المتضادة والخواص المتنافرة حتى في الحبة الواحدة لا يكون عن طبيعة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r4.speaker: الإمام الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r4.claim: Seeds differ in color and shape, each type has its own benefit, and a fruit may feed one animal but poison another; shared natural and celestial influences cannot account for this.
