BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r4.anchor: في كل نوع منها خاصية ومنفعة غير ما في الآخر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r5.speaker: الإمام الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r5.claim: Leaf veins branch into ever finer channels like spinal nerves, drawing fine earthly particles through narrow passages and revealing meticulous care in the design of a tree.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r5.anchor: وعن كل واحد منها خيوط أخرى أدق من الأولى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r6.speaker: الإمام الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r6.claim: The hierarchy of care rises from tree to plants, animals, and humans; plants and animals serve human bodily needs, while the body serves knowledge, love, and worship of God.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r6.anchor: إنما خلق الحيوان والنبات في هذا العالم ليكون غذاء ودواء

BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r7.speaker: الإمام الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r7.claim: Contemplating a leaf and tracing its order upward through the tree and beyond leads toward the ultimate purpose of knowledge and love in human souls and opens endless disclosures.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p677/r7.anchor: فسبيلك أن تنظر في ورقة الشجرة وتتأمل في تلك الأوتار ثم تترقى منها

DURR-FULL:v3p324/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the splitter of grain and date stones as their Creator.
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس في قوله

DURR-FULL:v3p324/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r3.claim: Qatada says God splits grain and date stones to bring forth vegetation.
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {فالق الحب والنوى} قال: يفلق الحب والنوى عن النبات

DURR-FULL:v3p324/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r4.claim: Mujahid takes the phrase to mean the two fissures within the grain and seed.
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {فالق الحب والنوى} قال: الشقان اللذان فيهما

DURR-FULL:v3p324/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r5.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r5.claim: Abu Malik identifies the split as the crack in the seed stone and wheat grain.
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r5.anchor: عن أبي مالك رضي الله عنه في قوله {فالق الحب والنوى} قال: الشق الذي

DURR-FULL:v3p324/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r6.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r6.claim: Al-Suddi explains that God splits the grain to bring out the ear and the date stone to bring out the palm.
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r6.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه في قوله {فالق الحب والنوى} قال: فالق الحبة عن السنبلة

DURR-FULL:v3p324/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r7.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r7.claim: Abu Malik illustrates life from death and death from life with a palm emerging from its seed and a seed from a palm, and an ear from grain and grain from an ear.
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r7.anchor: عن أبي مالك رضي الله عنه في قوله {يخرج الحي من الميت} قال: النخلة من النواة

DURR-FULL:v3p324/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r8.claim: Mujahid says living people emerge from dead sperm, while sperm comes from living people; the same pattern applies to livestock and plants.
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي} قال: الناس الأحياء

DURR-FULL:v3p324/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the question as asking how they can be deceived or lie.
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {فأنى تؤفكون} قال: كيف تكذبون

DURR-FULL:v3p324/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r10.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r10.claim: Hasan glosses the phrase as asking how they are turned away.
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r10.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {فأنى تؤفكون} قال: أنى تصرفون

DURR-FULL:v3p324/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r11.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r11.claim: Al-Suddi says the phrase asks how their minds can be turned away from recognizing this.
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r11.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {فأنى تؤفكون} قال: كيف تضل عقولكم عن هذا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r7.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r7.claim: When Umm Kulthum bint ʿUqba migrated to Medina and refused to return to the polytheists, the Prophet recited “He brings the living out of the dead” in a figurative application.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r7.anchor: ومن هذا قول النبي لأم كلثوم بنت عقبة بن معيط حين جاءت مسلمة مهاجرة إلى المدينة
